title.zh: 卷三百〇六 列傳第六十五 謝泌 孫何 朱台符 戚綸 張去華 樂黃目 柴成務
title.en: Volume 306 Biographies 65: Xie Bi, Sun He, Zhu Taifu, Qi Lun, Zhang Quhua, Le Huangmu, Chai Chengwu
title.raw: 卷三百〇六 列傳第六十五 謝泌 孫何 朱台符 戚綸 張去華 樂黃目 柴成務 Volume 306 Biographies 65: Xie Bi, Sun He, Zhu Taifu, Qi Lun, Zhang Quhua, Le Huangmu, Chai Chengwu

sentences.zh: 謝泌，字宗源，歙州歙人。

translations.literal: Xie Bi, style name Zongyuan, was a man of She [county] in She Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Bi, courtesy name Zongyuan, was a native of She County in She Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 自言晉太保安二十七世孫。

translations.literal: He himself said he was the twenty-seventh-generation descendant of [Xie] An, Duke of Tai'an of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed descent from Xie An, Duke of Tai'an of Jin, twenty-seven generations removed.

sentences.zh: 少好學，有志操。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning and had purposeful conduct.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he loved learning and possessed firm moral resolve.

sentences.zh: 賈黃中知宣州，一見奇之。

translations.literal: When Jia Huangzhong was prefect of Xuan [Prefecture], at one meeting he regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: When Jia Huangzhong served as prefect of Xuanzhou, he was struck by Bi at first sight.

sentences.zh: 太平興國五年進士，解褐大理評事、知清川縣，徙彰明，遷著作佐郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo he became a jinshi, doffed commoner's garb as investigating censor of the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Qingchuan County, was transferred to Zhangming, and promoted to Assistant Editorial Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo (980) he passed the jinshi examination, entered office as an investigating censor of the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Qingchuan County, was transferred to Zhangming, and promoted to Assistant Editorial Director.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，為殿中丞，獻所著文十編、《古今類要》三十卷，召試中書，以直史館賜緋。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he was Palace Attendant, presented ten compilations of his writings and thirty juan of Essentials Arranged by Category from Antiquity to the Present, was summoned for examination at the Secretariat, and was made a straight official of the Historiography Institute with crimson robes bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Duangong (988) he served as Palace Attendant, submitted ten volumes of his own writings and thirty juan of Essentials Arranged by Category from Antiquity to the Present, was summoned for examination at the Secretariat, and was appointed to the Historiography Institute with the gift of crimson robes.

sentences.zh: 時言事者眾，詔閣門，非涉僥望乃許受之，繇是言路稍壅。

translations.literal: At the time many were speaking on affairs; an edict to the Gate [of Acclamation] allowed acceptance only of those not involving improper hopes—thereby the avenue of speech was somewhat blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Many were then submitting memorials on affairs of state. An edict ordered the Gate of Acclamation to accept only those not involving improper solicitations, and the avenue for remonstrance was somewhat choked off.

sentences.zh: 泌抗疏陳其不可，且言：「邊鄙有事，民政未乂，狂夫之言，聖人擇焉。

translations.literal: Bi submitted a forthright memorial stating it could not be done, and said: 'The borderlands have affairs; civil administration is not yet settled—the madman's words, the sage selects from them.
translations.idiomatic: Bi submitted a forthright memorial arguing that this could not stand, saying: "The border regions are troubled and civil administration is not yet settled. Even a madman's words—the sage selects from them.

sentences.zh: 苟詰而拒之，四聰之明，將有所蔽。

translations.literal: If one interrogates and rejects them, the clarity of the Four Listeners will be somewhat obscured.
translations.idiomatic: If you interrogate and reject them outright, the clarity of your Four Listeners will be partly blinded.

sentences.zh: 願采其可者，拒其不可者，庶顒顒之情，得以上達。」

translations.literal: I pray that the acceptable be adopted and the unacceptable rejected, so that sincere sentiments may reach above.'
translations.idiomatic: Adopt what is sound and reject what is not, so that sincere feeling may reach you from below."

sentences.zh: 復言：「國家圖書，多失次序。

translations.literal: He again said: 'The state's books and documents are largely out of order.
translations.idiomatic: He went on: "The state's library holdings are largely disordered.

sentences.zh: 唐景龍中，嘗分經、史、子、集為四庫，命薛稷、沈佺期、武平一、馬懷素分掌，望遵復故事。」

translations.literal: In the Jinglong era of Tang, the classics, histories, masters, and collections were once divided into four repositories, with Xue Ji, Shen Quanqi, Wu Pingyi, and Ma Huaisu assigned to oversee each in turn—I hope the old precedent may be followed again.'
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang Jinglong (707–710), the classics, histories, masters, and collections were once divided into four repositories, with Xue Ji, Shen Quanqi, Wu Pingyi, and Ma Huaisu each put in charge. I ask that this precedent be restored."

sentences.zh: 遂令直館分典四部，以泌知集庫。

translations.literal: Thereupon straight officials of the institutes were ordered to oversee the four divisions separately, with Bi put in charge of the collection repository.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered straight officials of the institutes to oversee the four divisions separately, appointing Bi to manage the collection repository.

sentences.zh: 改左正言，使嶺南採訪。

translations.literal: He was changed to Left Rectifier and sent on an inspection tour of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Left Rectifier and dispatched on an inspection tour of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，久旱，復上言時政得失。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua, during prolonged drought, he again submitted memorials on the gains and losses of current policy.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua (991), amid a long drought, he again memorialized the court on the strengths and failings of current policy.

sentences.zh: 時王禹偁上言：「請自今庶官候謁宰相，並須朝罷於政事堂，樞密使預坐接見，將以杜私請。」

translations.literal: At the time Wang Yucheng memorialized: 'From now on, when lower officials wait to call on the chief ministers, they must all do so after court at the Hall of Administration, with the Commissioner of Military Affairs present and seated to receive them—this is intended to block private solicitations.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yucheng then memorialized: "From now on, when lower officials wait to call on the chief ministers, they must do so only at the Hall of Administration after court is dismissed, with the Commissioner of Military Affairs present and seated to receive them—this will cut off private solicitations."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved it by edict.

sentences.zh: 泌上言曰：「伏睹明詔，不許宰相、樞密使見賓客，是疑大臣以私也。

translations.literal: Bi memorialized: 'I have seen the illustrious edict forbidding chief ministers and commissioners of military affairs from seeing guests—it is to suspect the great ministers of private dealings.
translations.idiomatic: Bi memorialized: "I have read Your Majesty's edict forbidding chief ministers and commissioners of military affairs from receiving guests. This is to suspect your great ministers of private dealings.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：『任賢勿貳，去邪勿疑。』

translations.literal: The Documents says: 'Employ the worthy without duplicity; remove the wicked without hesitation.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: "Employ the worthy without duplicity; remove the wicked without hesitation."

sentences.zh: 張說謂姚元崇曰：『外則疏而接物，內則謹以事君。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue said to Yao Chong: 'Outwardly be open in receiving people; inwardly be careful in serving the ruler.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue told Yao Chong: "Outwardly be open in receiving people; inwardly be scrupulous in serving the ruler."

sentences.zh: 此真大臣之禮。』

translations.literal: This is truly the ritual of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: That is the true deportment of a great minister.

sentences.zh: 今天下至廣，萬機至繁，陛下以聰明寄於輔臣，自非接下，何以悉知外事？

translations.literal: Today the realm is vast and the myriad affairs extremely complex; Your Majesty entrusts your intelligence to assisting ministers—if they do not receive people below, how can they fully know external affairs?
translations.idiomatic: The realm is vast today and affairs of state exceedingly complex. Your Majesty entrusts your discernment to your assisting ministers; unless they receive people below, how can they fully know what is happening outside?

sentences.zh: 若令都堂候見，則庶官請見諮事，略無解衣之暇。

translations.literal: If they are made to wait for audiences at the chief hall, then when lower officials request audiences to consult on affairs, there will scarcely be leisure even to loosen one's robe.
translations.idiomatic: If all audiences must wait at the chief hall, lower officials seeking meetings to consult on business will leave the ministers no moment even to loosen their robes.

sentences.zh: 今陛下囊括宇宙，總攬英豪，朝廷無巧言之士，方面無姑息之臣，奈何疑執政，為衰世之事乎！

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty embraces heaven and earth and gathers heroes; at court there are no crafty speakers, in the regions no indulgent ministers—why suspect those in power and do what belongs to a declining age!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty now embraces the realm and gathers the able; at court there are no crafty tongues, in the provinces no indulgent officials. Why suspect those who govern and adopt the practices of a declining age?

sentences.zh: 王禹偁昧於大體，妄有陳述。」

translations.literal: Wang Yucheng was blind to the larger pattern and rashly made this proposal.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yucheng failed to grasp the larger pattern and rashly made this proposal."

sentences.zh: 太宗覽奏，即追還前詔，仍以泌所上表送史館。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong read the memorial, immediately recalled the previous edict, and also sent Bi's submitted memorial to the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong read the memorial, he immediately revoked the earlier edict and had Bi's memorial sent to the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 會修正殿，頗施采繪，泌復上疏，亟命代以丹堊，且嘉其忠藎，拜左司諫，賜金紫、錢三十萬。

translations.literal: When the Hall of Rectification was being repaired with considerable painted ornament, Bi again submitted a memorial; [the emperor] urgently ordered it replaced with cinnabar whitewash, and in praise of his loyal devotion appointed him Left Bureau Remonstrator, bestowing gold-and-purple [robes] and three hundred thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hall of Rectification was being refurbished with elaborate painting, Bi memorialized again; the emperor promptly ordered plain cinnabar whitewash instead, praised his loyal devotion, appointed him Left Bureau Remonstrator, and granted him gold-and-purple insignia and three hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 一日，得對便殿，太宗稱其任直敢言，泌奏曰：「陛下從諫如流，故臣得以竭誠。

translations.literal: One day he was received in audience at the side hall; Taizong praised his straightforwardness and bold speech. Bi submitted: 'Your Majesty accepts remonstrance as flowing water—therefore your servant has been able to exhaust his sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: One day he was received in audience at the side hall. Taizong praised his forthrightness and bold speech. Bi said: "Your Majesty accepts remonstrance as flowing water; that is why your servant has been able to speak with full sincerity.

sentences.zh: 昔唐季孟昌圖者，朝疏諫而夕去位，鑒於前代，取亂宜矣。」

translations.literal: In the late Tang, Meng Changtu memorialized in the morning with remonstrance and by evening had lost his post—taking warning from former ages, disorder was fitting.'
translations.idiomatic: In late Tang, Meng Changtu remonstrated in a morning memorial and lost his post by evening. Taking warning from former ages, disorder was only to be expected."

sentences.zh: 太宗動色久之。

translations.literal: Taizong's expression changed for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's expression changed, and he was silent for a long while.

sentences.zh: 時，群臣升殿言事者，既可其奏，得專達於有司，頗容巧妄，泌請自今凡政事送中書，機事送樞密，金穀送三司，覆奏而行，從之。

translations.literal: At the time, when ministers ascending the hall to speak on affairs had their memorials approved, they could transmit directly to the relevant offices—this rather allowed craft and falsehood. Bi requested that from now on all government affairs go to the Secretariat, military affairs to the Bureau of Military Affairs, and funds and grain to the Three Offices, with memorials returned for approval before execution. This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, when ministers who spoke on affairs in court had their proposals approved, they could transmit them directly to the relevant offices, which rather encouraged craft and falsehood. Bi asked that henceforth government affairs go to the Secretariat, military affairs to the Bureau of Military Affairs, and fiscal matters to the Three Offices, with everything returned for imperial approval before execution. The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 俄判三司鹽鐵勾院。

translations.literal: Shortly he was assigned to judge the Salt and Iron Audit Office of the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was assigned to the Salt and Iron Audit Office of the Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 奉詔解送國學舉人，黜落既多，群聚喧詬，懷甓以伺泌出，泌知之，潛由他塗入史館，數宿不敢出，請對自陳，太宗問：「何官騶導嚴肅，都人畏避？」

translations.literal: By imperial order he escorted candidates of the National University; many were failed, and they gathered in a crowd shouting abuse, carrying bricks to wait for Bi to come out. Bi learned of this, secretly entered the Historiography Institute by another route, and for several nights dared not go out. He requested audience to state his case himself. Taizong asked: 'What office has such solemn outriders that the capital's people fear and avoid them?'
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he escorted National University candidates; many were failed, and they gathered shouting abuse, carrying bricks to waylay him when he came out. Bi learned of this, slipped into the Historiography Institute by another route, and for several nights dared not leave. He requested a private audience to explain himself. Taizong asked: "Which office has outriders so imposing that people in the capital fear and avoid them?"

sentences.zh: 有以臺雜對者，即授泌虞部員外郎兼侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: Someone answered that it was the censorate's supervising censor—thereupon Bi was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and Concurrent Attending Censor with charge of miscellaneous censorial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Someone replied that it was the supervising censor of the censorate, and Bi was immediately appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Works with concurrent appointment as Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous censorial affairs.

sentences.zh: 上元觀燈，泌特預召，自是為例。

translations.literal: At the Lantern Festival of the first month, Bi was specially summoned in advance—thereafter this became precedent.
translations.idiomatic: At the First Month Lantern Festival, Bi was specially summoned in advance, and this thereafter became precedent.

sentences.zh: 轉金部員外郎，充鹽鐵副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and served as deputy commissioner of salt and iron.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and served as deputy commissioner of salt and iron.

sentences.zh: 頃之，魏羽為使，即泌之外舅，以親嫌，改度支副使。

translations.literal: Before long Wei Yu served as commissioner—he was Bi's maternal uncle—so on grounds of kinship Bi was changed to deputy commissioner of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wei Yu became commissioner; he was Bi's maternal uncle, so on grounds of kinship Bi was reassigned as deputy commissioner of revenue.

sentences.zh: 因郊祀，條上軍士賞給之數，太宗曰：「朕惜金帛，止備賞賜爾。」

translations.literal: On the occasion of suburban sacrifice he itemized the numbers for soldiers' rewards and grants. Taizong said: 'I am sparing of gold and silk—it is only to prepare for rewards.'
translations.idiomatic: On the occasion of the suburban sacrifice he itemized the numbers for soldiers' rewards and grants. Taizong said: "I am sparing of gold and silk—it is only to have enough for rewards."

sentences.zh: 泌因曰：「唐德宗朱泚之亂、後唐莊宗馬射之禍，皆賞軍不豐所致。

translations.literal: Bi thereupon said: 'The rebellion of Zhu Ci under Tang Dezong and the disaster of horse archery under Later Tang Zhuangzong were both caused by insufficient rewards to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Bi replied: "The rebellion of Zhu Ci under Tang Dezong and the disaster at the horse archery grounds under Later Tang Zhuangzong both came from rewarding the army too meagerly.

sentences.zh: 今陛下薄於躬御，賞賜特優，實歷代之所難也。」

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty is sparing in personal expenditure while rewards are especially generous—this is truly what former ages found difficult.'
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is frugal in personal expenditure while your rewards are especially generous—something truly difficult for any previous age to match."

sentences.zh: 俄與王沔同磨勘京朝官。

translations.literal: Shortly he joined Wang Han in reviewing capital metropolitan officials.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he joined Wang Han in reviewing metropolitan officials at the capital.

sentences.zh: 太宗孜孜為治，每御長春殿視事罷，復即崇政殿臨決，日旰未進御膳。

translations.literal: Taizong was diligent in governing; each time he finished conducting affairs at the Hall of Everlasting Spring, he would again go to the Hall of Esteeming Government to decide cases, and at sundown had still not taken the imperial meal.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was tireless in governing. Each day after finishing business at the Hall of Everlasting Spring, he would go straight to the Hall of Esteeming Government to decide cases, and at sundown had still not taken his meal.

sentences.zh: 泌言：「請自今長春罷政，既膳後御便坐。」

translations.literal: Bi said: 'From now on, when affairs end at Everlasting Spring, after the meal take the informal seat.'
translations.idiomatic: Bi said: "From now on, when business ends at the Hall of Everlasting Spring, take your meal first, then hold court at the informal seat."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not respond.

sentences.zh: 俄知三班、通進銀臺司，出知湖州。

translations.literal: Shortly he was put in charge of the Three Ranks and the Office for Transmission and the Silver Terrace, then went out as prefect of Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was put in charge of the Three Ranks and the Office for Transmission and the Silver Terrace, then sent out as prefect of Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 再遷主客郎中、知虢州。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Director of the Bureau of Receptions and made prefect of Guo [Prefecture].
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Director of the Bureau of Receptions and appointed prefect of Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 真宗初，邊人屢寇，泌上疏曰：

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenzong's reign, border peoples repeatedly raided; Bi submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Zhenzong's reign, border peoples raided repeatedly. Bi submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 「臣竊惟聖心所切者，欲天下朝夕太平爾。

translations.literal: 'Your servant ventures to consider that what the sage heart most desires is that the realm be at peace morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: "Your servant ventures to believe that what weighs on Your Majesty's mind is the wish that the realm may be at peace morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 雍熙末，趙普錄唐姚崇《太平十事》以獻。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongxi, Zhao Pu copied Yao Chong's Ten Matters for Great Peace of Tang and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yongxi (987), Zhao Pu copied Yao Chong's Ten Matters for Great Peace from Tang and presented them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 未幾，普復相，時稱致治之策無出於此。

translations.literal: Before long Zhao Pu again became chief minister; at the time it was said that policies for achieving good order had nothing beyond this.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhao Pu returned as chief minister, and at the time it was said that no policy for achieving good order surpassed this.

sentences.zh: 尋普病，又遼騎擾邊，因循未行。

translations.literal: Soon Zhao Pu fell ill, and again Liao horsemen disturbed the border—matters dragged on and were not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhao Pu fell ill, and Liao horsemen again disturbed the border, so the plan was put off and never carried out.

sentences.zh: 今北邊謐寧，繼遷請命，則可行於今日矣。

translations.literal: Now the northern border is tranquil and Jiqian has submitted to command—then it may be carried out today.
translations.idiomatic: Now the northern border is tranquil and Jiqian has submitted. The plan can be carried out today.

sentences.zh: 臣以為先朝未盡行者，俟陛下爾。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that what the former court did not fully carry out awaits Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant believes that what the former court left unfinished awaits Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 陛下自臨大寶，邊不加兵，西北肅然，民安歲登，則太平之象，復何遠哉。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty ascended the great treasure, troops have not been added at the border; the northwest is orderly; the people are secure and harvests abundant—then the signs of great peace, how far off can they be?
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, you have not added troops at the border; the northwest is orderly; the people are secure and harvests abundant. How far off can the signs of great peace be?

sentences.zh: 至於省不急之務，削煩苛之政，抑奔競，來直言，斯皆致太平之術，又豈讓唐開元之治也。

translations.literal: As for reducing non-urgent affairs, cutting vexatious and harsh government, restraining frantic competition, and welcoming straight speech—all these are methods for achieving great peace. How could one yield to the governance of Tang Kaiyuan?
translations.idiomatic: Reduce non-urgent business, cut vexatious and harsh policies, restrain frantic competition, and welcome frank speech—these are all methods for achieving great peace. Why should we yield even to the Kaiyuan reign of Tang?

sentences.zh: 議者或謂，方今用兵異於開元，且開元邊戎孔熾，明皇卒與之和。

translations.literal: Some in discussion say that using troops today differs from Kaiyuan, and moreover that under Kaiyuan border barbarians were intensely active and Ming Huang ultimately made peace with them.
translations.idiomatic: Some argue that using troops today differs from Kaiyuan, and that under Kaiyuan border enemies were fiercely active until Emperor Ming finally made peace with them.

sentences.zh: 至如漢高祖亦然。

translations.literal: The same was true of Han Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: The same was true of Emperor Gaozu of Han.

sentences.zh: 此皆屈己以寧天下，豈以輕大國而競小忿乎。

translations.literal: These all bent themselves to settle the realm—how could one slight a great state to contend over small resentments?
translations.idiomatic: These rulers humbled themselves to settle the realm. How could one slight a great state to contend over small resentments?

sentences.zh: 請以近事言，往歲討交阯，王師一動，南方幾搖。

translations.literal: Allow me to speak from recent events: in past years when Jiaozhi was attacked, once the imperial army moved, the south nearly shook.
translations.idiomatic: Consider recent events: when Jiaozhi was attacked in past years, the moment the imperial army moved, the south nearly came apart.

sentences.zh: 先皇以為得之無用，棄之實便，及授官為蕃屏，則至今鼠伏。

translations.literal: The late emperor considered that gaining it was useless and abandoning it was truly convenient; when offices were granted to make them a border screen, to this day they crouch like rats.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor judged that taking it would be useless and abandoning it the wiser course. Once offices were granted to make them a border screen, they have crouched like mice to this day.

sentences.zh: 石晉之末，恥講和契丹，遂致天下橫流，豈得為強？

translations.literal: At the end of Later Jin, they were ashamed to make peace with the Khitan, and thereby caused the realm to flow sideways—how could that be called strength?
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Later Jin, shame at making peace with the Khitan led the realm into chaos. How could that be called strength?

sentences.zh: 或者有言，敵所嗜者禽色，所貪者財利，餘無他智計。

translations.literal: Some say the enemy's loves are birds and beauty, their greed is for wealth and profit—beyond this they have no other schemes.
translations.idiomatic: Some say the enemy cares only for birds and beauty, covets only wealth and profit, and has no other stratagems.

sentences.zh: 先朝平晉之後，若不舉兵臨之，但與財帛，則幽薊不日納土矣。

translations.literal: After the former court pacified Jin, if they had not raised troops against them but only given wealth and silk, You and Ji would have submitted their territory within days.
translations.idiomatic: After the former court pacified Jin, if it had not marched against them but only sent wealth and silk, You and Ji would have submitted within days.

sentences.zh: 察此，乃知其情古猶今也、漢祖、明皇所用之計，正可以餌其心矣。

translations.literal: Observing this, one knows their disposition is the same in antiquity as today; the stratagems used by Han's founding emperor and Tang's Ming Emperor can precisely bait their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: From this one sees their disposition is the same in antiquity as today. The stratagems used by Emperor Gaozu of Han and Emperor Ming of Tang can precisely be used to bait their hearts.

sentences.zh: 臣伏睹近詔，以不逞之徒所陳述，皆閭閻事。

translations.literal: Your servant has seen the recent edict that what the unruly submit is all neighborhood affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has read the recent edict treating what unruly petitioners submit as mere neighborhood affairs.

sentences.zh: 臣聞古先哲王詢於芻蕘，察於邇言者，蓋慮視聽之蔽，故采此以達物情，亦罕行其事也。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that ancient sage kings inquired of grass cutters and examined nearby words because they feared blindness of sight and hearing—therefore they adopted these to reach the feelings of things, yet rarely carried out what was said.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient sage kings inquired even of grass cutters and weighed nearby words because they feared their sight and hearing might be blocked. They took such counsel to learn how things stood below, yet rarely acted on it.

sentences.zh: 先朝有侯莫陳利用、陳廷山、鄭昌嗣、趙贊之徒，喋喋利口，賴先帝聖聰，尋翦除之，然為患已深矣。

translations.literal: The former court had Hou Mo Chen Liyong, Chen Tingshan, Zheng Changsi, Zhao Zan, and the like—chattering with sharp tongues. Thanks to the late emperor's sage intelligence they were soon cut down, yet the harm had already been deep.
translations.idiomatic: The former court had men such as Hou Mo Chen Liyong, Chen Tingshan, Zheng Changsi, and Zhao Zan—glib and sharp-tongued. Thanks to the late emperor's discernment they were soon removed, but the harm had already run deep.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞輔時佐主，建萬世之基，立不拔之策者，必倚老成之人。

translations.literal: Your servant has also heard that those who assist the times and aid the ruler, establishing foundations for ten thousand generations and setting policies that cannot be uprooted, must rely on seasoned elders.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has also heard that those who assist their age and ruler, lay foundations for ten thousand generations, and set policies that cannot be uprooted must rely on seasoned elders.

sentences.zh: 至如成、康刑措，由任周、召；

translations.literal: As for Cheng and Kang, when punishments were set aside—it was through employing the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao;
translations.idiomatic: When punishments were set aside under Cheng and Kang, it was because the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao were employed;

sentences.zh: 文、景清靜，不易蕭、曹；

translations.literal: the quiet governance of Wen and Jing did not change Xiao and Cao;
translations.idiomatic: the quiet governance of Wen and Jing did not displace Xiao He and Cao Shen;

sentences.zh: 明皇太平，亦資姚、宋。

translations.literal: Ming Huang's great peace also relied on Yao and Song.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming's age of great peace likewise depended on Yao Chong and Song Jing.

sentences.zh: 夫精練國政，斟酌王度，未聞市井之胥，走塵之吏，可當其任也。

translations.literal: As for mastering state affairs and weighing royal measures, one has not heard that marketplace clerks and dust-chasing petty officials could fill such posts.
translations.idiomatic: To master state affairs and weigh imperial policy—one has never heard that marketplace clerks and petty runners could fill such posts.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下察往古用賢致治之道，則賢者亦必盡忠竭力，以輔成太平之治矣。」

translations.literal: Only if Your Majesty examines the way of employing the worthy to achieve good order in former ages will the worthy also surely exhaust loyalty and effort to assist in completing the governance of great peace.'
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty examines how former ages employed the worthy to achieve good order, the worthy will surely exhaust their loyalty and effort to help bring about an age of great peace."

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，徙知同州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping he was transferred to be prefect of Tong [Prefecture].
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianping (999) he was transferred to prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 代還，知鼓司、登聞院。

translations.literal: When replaced and returned, he was put in charge of the Drum Office and the Court of Imperial Complaints.
translations.idiomatic: When his replacement arrived and he returned to court, he was put in charge of the Drum Office and the Court of Imperial Complaints.

sentences.zh: 五年，與陳恕同知貢舉，復知通進銀臺司，加刑部，出為兩浙轉運使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he joined Chen Shu in supervising the civil examinations, again took charge of the Office for Transmission and the Silver Terrace, was given additional rank in the Ministry of Punishments, and went out as transport commissioner of the Two Zhes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he joined Chen Shu in supervising the civil examinations, again took charge of the Office for Transmission and the Silver Terrace, received additional rank in the Ministry of Punishments, and was sent out as transport commissioner of the Two Zhes.

sentences.zh: 近制，文武官告老皆遷秩，令錄授朝官，並給半俸。

translations.literal: Under recent regulations, when civil and military officials reported old age they were all promoted in rank; clerks were granted metropolitan official rank and all given half salary.
translations.idiomatic: Under recent regulations, when civil and military officials retired on grounds of age they were all promoted in rank; clerks were granted metropolitan official rank and all received half salary.

sentences.zh: 泌言：「請自今七十以上求退者，許致仕；

translations.literal: Bi said: 'From now on, those seventy and above who seek to retire—permit them to resign office;
translations.idiomatic: Bi said: "From now on, let those seventy and above who seek to retire be permitted to resign office;

sentences.zh: 因疾及歷任犯贓者，聽從便。」

translations.literal: those who retire due to illness or who in service committed graft—let them do as they please.'
translations.idiomatic: those who retire due to illness or who committed graft while in office may do as they please."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved it by edict.

sentences.zh: 徙知福州，代還，民懷其愛，刻石以紀去思。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be prefect of Fuzhou; when replaced and returned, the people cherished his kindness and carved stone to record their sorrow at his departure.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Fuzhou. When his replacement arrived, the people cherished him and carved a stone to commemorate his departure.

sentences.zh: 轉兵部郎中，復知審官院，直昭文館。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, again put in charge of the Bureau for Reviewing Appointments, and made a straight official of the Hall of Illustrious Culture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, again put in charge of the Bureau for Reviewing Appointments, and made a straight official of the Hall of Illustrious Culture.

sentences.zh: 知荊南府，改襄州，遷太常少卿、右諫議大夫、判吏部銓。

translations.literal: He was prefect of Jingnan Circuit, changed to Xiang [Prefecture], promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Right Remonstrance Grand Master, and assigned to judge the Ministry of Personnel's selection.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Jingnan Circuit, was transferred to Xiangzhou, and was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Right Remonstrance Grand Master, with assignment to judge selections at the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符五年卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died, age sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu (1012), at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 泌性端直，然好方外之學，疾革，服道士服，端坐死。

translations.literal: Bi's nature was upright, yet he loved learning beyond the world. When his illness became critical, he donned Daoist robes and died sitting upright.
translations.idiomatic: Bi was upright by nature, yet he loved Daoist learning. When his illness became critical, he put on Daoist robes and died sitting upright.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而嗟異，遣使臨問恤賜，錄其子衍為太常寺奉禮郎，衒將作監主簿。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and sighed in wonder, sent envoys to inquire in person and grant condolence gifts, and enrolled his sons Yan as Ceremonial Officer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Xuan as Chief Clerk of the Directorate of Imperial Works.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard this he sighed in wonder, sent envoys to offer condolences and grants, and enrolled his sons Yan as Ceremonial Officer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Xuan as Chief Clerk of the Directorate of Imperial Works.

sentences.zh: 衍為太子中舍。

translations.literal: Yan became Palace Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Yan later became Palace Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 孫何，字漢公，蔡州汝陽人。

translations.literal: Sun He, style name Hangong, was a man of Ruyang in Cai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sun He, courtesy name Hangong, was a native of Ruyang in Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 祖鎰，唐末秦宗權據州，強以賓佐起之。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yi—in late Tang when Qin Zongquan held the prefecture—was forcibly raised as a guest and aide.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yi, in late Tang when Qin Zongquan seized the prefecture, was forcibly pressed into service as a staff adviser.

sentences.zh: 鎰偽疾不應，還家，以講授為業。

translations.literal: Yi feigned illness and did not respond, returned home, and made lecturing his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Yi feigned illness and refused, returned home, and made a living by teaching.

sentences.zh: 父庸，字鼎臣，顯德中，獻《贊聖策》九篇，引唐貞觀所行事，以魏元成自況。

translations.literal: His father Yong, style name Dingchen—in Xiande presented nine chapters of Strategies Praising the Sage, citing what was done in Tang Zhenguan and comparing himself to Wei Yuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yong, courtesy name Dingchen, during Xiande (954–959) presented nine chapters of Strategies Praising the Sage, citing precedents from Tang Zhenguan and comparing himself to Wei Yuancheng.

sentences.zh: 得對，言曰：「武不可黷，斂不可厚，奢不可放，欲不可極。」

translations.literal: He gained audience and said: 'War must not be abused; levies must not be heavy; extravagance must not be indulged; desires must not be carried to extremes.'
translations.idiomatic: He gained an audience and said: "War must not be abused, levies must not be heavy, extravagance must not be indulged, and desires must not be carried to extremes."

sentences.zh: 世宗奇其言，命中書試，補開封兵曹掾。

translations.literal: Shizong marveled at his words, ordered examination at the Secretariat, and appointed him Clerk of the Military Section of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong marveled at his words, ordered him examined at the Secretariat, and appointed him clerk of the military section in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 建隆初，為河南簿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianlong he was registrar of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianlong (960) he served as registrar of Henan.

sentences.zh: 太平興國六年，鴻臚少卿劉章薦其材，改左贊善大夫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taiping Xingguo, Vice Director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception Liu Zhang recommended his talent, and he was changed to Left Supporter of Goodness Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taiping Xingguo (981), Vice Director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception Liu Zhang recommended his talent, and he was promoted to Left Supporter of Goodness Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 歷殿中丞、知龍州而卒。

translations.literal: He passed through Palace Attendant and prefect of Long [Prefecture], then died.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Palace Attendant and prefect of Longzhou, then died.

sentences.zh: 何十歲識音韻，十五能屬文，篤學嗜古，為文必本經義，在貢籍中甚有聲。

translations.literal: He at age ten knew phonology and rhyme; at fifteen could compose prose. He studied deeply and loved antiquity; in writing he always grounded himself in canonical meaning, and among examination candidates had great renown.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he knew phonology and rhyme; at fifteen he could compose prose. He studied deeply and loved antiquity, always grounding his writing in canonical meaning, and was highly regarded among examination candidates.

sentences.zh: 與丁謂齊名友善，時輩號為「孫丁」。

translations.literal: He was equally famed and friendly with Ding Wei; contemporaries called them 'Sun and Ding.'
translations.idiomatic: He was equally famed and on friendly terms with Ding Wei; contemporaries called them "Sun and Ding."

sentences.zh: 王禹偁尤雅重之。

translations.literal: Wang Yucheng especially esteemed him with refined regard.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yucheng especially esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 嘗作《兩晉名臣贊》、《宋詩》二十篇、《春秋意》、《尊儒教儀》，聞於時。

translations.literal: He once composed Eulogies of Famous Ministers of the Two Jins, twenty chapters of Song Poetry, Intentions of the Spring and Autumn, and Rites for Honoring Confucian Teaching—all renowned in his time.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Eulogies of Famous Ministers of the Two Jin Dynasties, twenty chapters of Song Poetry, Intentions of the Spring and Autumn Annals, and Rites for Honoring Confucian Teaching, all of which were well known in his day.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年舉進士，開封府、禮部俱首薦，及第又得甲科，解褐將作監丞、通判陝州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunhua he passed the jinshi examination; both Kaifeng Prefecture and the Ministry of Rites recommended him first; upon passing he also received first rank, and upon doffing commoner's robes was appointed Assistant Director of the Directorate of Works and Vice Administrator of Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chunhua (990) he passed the jinshi examination, earning top recommendation from both Kaifeng Prefecture and the Ministry of Rites; he graduated in first rank and, upon entering office, was appointed Assistant Director of the Directorate of Works and Vice Administrator of Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 召入直史館，賜緋，遷秘書丞、京西轉運副使。

translations.literal: He was summoned to serve in the Historiography Institute, granted crimson robes, and promoted to Secretary of the Palace Library and Vice Commissioner of the Western Capital Transport Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the Historiography Institute, granted crimson robes, and promoted to Secretary of the Palace Library and Vice Commissioner of the Western Capital Transport Circuit.

sentences.zh: 歷右正言，改右司諫。

translations.literal: He served as Right Remonstrance Officer, then was changed to Right Office Remonstrance Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Right Remonstrance Officer and was then transferred to Right Office Remonstrance Censor.

sentences.zh: 真宗初，何獻五議：其一，請擇儒臣有方略者統兵；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenzong's reign, He submitted five proposals: first, he requested that Confucian officials with strategic ability be selected to command troops;
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Zhenzong's reign, Sun He submitted five proposals. First, he asked that Confucian officials with strategic ability be chosen to command troops;

sentences.zh: 其二，請世祿之家肄業太學，寒雋之士州郡推薦，而禁投贄自媒者；

translations.literal: second, he requested that hereditary salary families study at the Imperial Academy, talented poor scholars be recommended by prefectures and counties, and those who presented gifts to promote themselves be prohibited;
translations.idiomatic: second, that families holding hereditary salaries send their sons to study at the Imperial Academy, that talented men of humble birth be recommended by prefectures and counties, and that presenting gifts for self-promotion be forbidden;

sentences.zh: 其三，請復制舉；

translations.literal: third, he requested restoration of the special examination system;
translations.idiomatic: third, that the special examination system be restored;

sentences.zh: 其四，請行鄉飲酒禮；

translations.literal: fourth, he requested implementation of the village drinking ceremony;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, that the village drinking ceremony be observed;

sentences.zh: 其五，請以能授官，勿以恩慶例遷。

translations.literal: fifth, he requested that offices be granted based on ability, not by courtesy promotion through imperial grace.
translations.idiomatic: fifth, that offices be granted according to merit and not by courtesy promotion through imperial grace.

sentences.zh: 上覽而善之。

translations.literal: The emperor read them and approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read them and approved.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，舉入閣故事，何次當待制，獻疏曰：

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping, when the old custom of entering the inner hall was observed, it was He's turn as Attendant Drafter, and he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianping (999), when the old custom of entering the inner hall was observed, it was Sun He's turn as Attendant Drafter, and he submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 「六卿分職，邦家之大柄也。

translations.literal: "The Six Ministers divide duties—this is the great control of the state.
translations.idiomatic: "When the Six Ministers divide their duties, the great reins of the state are in hand.

sentences.zh: 有吏部辨考績而育人材，有兵部簡車徒而治戎備，有戶部正版圖而阜貨財，有刑部謹紀律而誅暴強，有禮部祀神示而選賢俊，有工部繕宮室而修堤防，六職舉而天下之事備矣。

translations.literal: There is the Ministry of Personnel to examine merit and cultivate talent; the Ministry of War to select chariots and troops and manage military preparations; the Ministry of Revenue to correct registers and maps and enrich goods and wealth; the Ministry of Justice to strictly maintain discipline and punish the violent and strong; the Ministry of Rites to sacrifice to the gods and display propriety and select worthy talents; the Ministry of Works to repair palaces and maintain dikes and embankments—when these six duties are fulfilled, affairs under Heaven are complete.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel examines merit and cultivates talent; the Ministry of War selects chariots and troops and keeps military readiness; the Ministry of Revenue corrects registers and maps and enriches the treasury; the Ministry of Justice upholds discipline and punishes the violent; the Ministry of Rites sacrifices to the gods, displays propriety, and selects worthy men; the Ministry of Works repairs palaces and maintains dikes and embankments. When these six offices perform their functions, nothing under Heaven is left undone.

sentences.zh: 故周之會府，漢之尚書，立庶政之根本，提百司之綱紀。

translations.literal: Therefore the Zhou Grand Secretariat and the Han Imperial Secretariat established the foundation of general administration and upheld the laws and standards of the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the Zhou Grand Secretariat and the Han Imperial Secretariat laid the foundation of government and held the laws and standards of the hundred offices.

sentences.zh: 令、僕率其屬，丞、郎分其行，二十四司粲焉星拱，郎中、員外判其曹，主事、令史承其事。

translations.literal: Ministers and Vice Ministers lead their subordinates; Directors and Gentlemen divide their functions; the twenty-four bureaus shine like stars arrayed around the pole; Bureau Chiefs and Vice Bureau Chiefs adjudicate their sections; Principal Clerks and Record Clerks carry out the business.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers and Vice Ministers lead their subordinates; Directors and Gentlemen divide the work; the twenty-four bureaus stand bright as stars around the pole; Bureau Chiefs and Vice Bureau Chiefs decide the affairs of their sections; Principal Clerks and Record Clerks carry out the tasks.

sentences.zh: 四海九州之大，若網在綱。

translations.literal: For the vast realm of the Four Seas and Nine Provinces, it is as if a net were held by its cord.
translations.idiomatic: Across the vast realm of the Four Seas and Nine Provinces, all is governed as a net is governed by its cord.

sentences.zh: 唐之盛時，亦不聞別分利權，創使額，而軍須取足。

translations.literal: Even in Tang's flourishing age, one never heard of separately dividing fiscal authority and creating commissioner posts, yet military needs were fully supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Even at the height of Tang, one never heard of splitting fiscal authority or creating special commissioner posts, yet military needs were fully met.

sentences.zh: 及玄宗侈心既萌，召發既廣，租調不充，於是蕭景、楊釗始以地官判度支，而宇文融為租調地稅使，始開利孔，以構禍階。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong's extravagant heart had already stirred and conscriptions had grown broad, land tax and corvée no longer sufficed—then Xiao Jing and Yang Zhao first had the Minister of Revenue adjudicate fiscal affairs, and Yuwen Rong became Commissioner for Land Tax and Corvée Tax, opening the fount of profit and laying the steps of disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Xuanzong's appetite for extravagance had awakened and conscription had grown vast, land tax and corvée no longer sufficed. Then Xiao Jing and Yang Zhao first had the Minister of Revenue take charge of fiscal affairs, and Yuwen Rong became Commissioner for Land Tax and Corvée Tax—opening the sluice of profit and laying the steps to disaster.

sentences.zh: 至於肅、代，則有司之職盡廢，而言利之臣攘臂於其間矣。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperors Suzong and Daizong, the duties of the regular offices were wholly abandoned, and ministers who spoke of profit thrust themselves forward among them.
translations.idiomatic: By the reigns of Emperors Suzong and Daizong, the duties of the regular offices had been wholly abandoned, and ministers who spoke of profit thrust themselves forward in their place.

sentences.zh: 於是叛亂相仍，經費不充，迫於軍期，切於國計，用救當時之急，率以權宜裁之。

translations.literal: Then rebellions followed one after another, funds were insufficient, pressed by military deadlines and urgent national finances, to rescue the emergency of the time they generally disposed of matters by expedient measures.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellions then followed one after another, funds ran short, and pressed by military deadlines and urgent state finances, the court, to meet the crisis of the moment, generally handled affairs by expedient measures.

sentences.zh: 五代短促，曾莫是思。

translations.literal: The Five Dynasties were brief—one scarcely gave this thought.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Dynasties were brief, and scarcely anyone gave this any thought.

sentences.zh: 今國家三聖相承，五兵不試，太平之業，垂統立制，在此時也。

translations.literal: Now the state has three sage emperors succeeding one another, the five weapons untried—in establishing the enterprise of peace and setting institutions for transmission, this is the time.
translations.idiomatic: Now the state has had three sage emperors succeed one another, and the five weapons have gone untried. To establish the work of peace and set institutions for generations to come—this is the moment.

sentences.zh: 所宜三部使額，還之六卿，慎擇戶部尚書一人，專掌鹽鐵使事，俾金部郎中、員外郎判之。

translations.literal: What is appropriate is to return the three-commissioner posts to the Six Ministers, carefully select one Minister of Revenue to exclusively manage Salt and Iron Commissioner affairs, and have Bureau Chiefs and Vice Bureau Chiefs of the Gold Section adjudicate them.
translations.idiomatic: The proper course is to return the three commissioner posts to the Six Ministers, carefully choose one Minister of Revenue to take exclusive charge of Salt and Iron Commissioner affairs, and have the Bureau Chiefs and Vice Bureau Chiefs of the Gold Section adjudicate them.

sentences.zh: 又擇本行侍郎二人，分掌度支、戶部使事，各以本曹郎中、員外郎分判之，則三使洎判官，雖省猶不省也。

translations.literal: Also select two Vice Ministers of the same ministry to separately manage Fiscal Affairs and Revenue Commissioner affairs, each with their own Bureau Chiefs and Vice Bureau Chiefs adjudicating—then the three commissioners together with their adjunct officials, though reduced, would not truly be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Choose as well two Vice Ministers of the same ministry to manage Fiscal Affairs and Revenue Commissioner affairs separately, each with Bureau Chiefs and Vice Bureau Chiefs of the relevant section to adjudicate them. Then the three commissioners and their adjunct officials, though nominally reduced, would in substance not be reduced at all.

sentences.zh: 仍命左右司郎中、員外總知帳目，分勾稽違。

translations.literal: Also order the Left and Right Office Bureau Chiefs and Vice Bureau Chiefs to oversee accounts in general and separately audit violations.
translations.idiomatic: Also appoint the Left and Right Office Bureau Chiefs and Vice Bureau Chiefs to oversee the accounts in general and separately audit violations.

sentences.zh: 職守有常，規程既定，則進無掊克之慮，退有詳練之名，周官唐式，可以復矣。

translations.literal: When duties have constants and regulations are fixed, then in advance there is no fear of extortion, and in retreat there is a name for thorough competence—the Zhou offices and Tang procedures can be restored.
translations.idiomatic: When duties are fixed and regulations established, there will be no fear of extortion going forward and a reputation for thorough competence behind—then the offices of Zhou and the procedures of Tang can be restored.

sentences.zh: 茲事非艱，在陛下行之爾。」

translations.literal: This matter is not difficult; it lies only in Your Majesty carrying it out."
translations.idiomatic: This is not a difficult matter. It depends only on Your Majesty putting it into practice."

sentences.zh: 是冬，從幸大名，詔訪邊事。

translations.literal: That winter, he accompanied the emperor on a visit to Daming; an edict sought inquiries on border affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he accompanied the emperor on a visit to Daming, and an edict called for inquiries on border affairs.

sentences.zh: 何疏曰：

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 「陛下嗣位以來，訓師擇將，可謂至多，以高祖之大度，兼蕭王之赤心，神武冠於百王，精兵倍於前代。

translations.literal: "Since Your Majesty succeeded to the throne, you have trained armies and selected generals—this can be called abundant; with the magnanimity of Emperor Gaozu and the loyal heart of Prince Xiao, divine martial prowess crowns the hundred kings, and elite troops double those of former ages.
translations.idiomatic: "Since Your Majesty succeeded to the throne, you have trained armies and chosen generals in abundance. With the magnanimity of Emperor Gaozu and the loyal heart of Prince Xiao, your divine martial prowess surpasses that of the hundred kings, and your elite troops are twice those of former ages.

sentences.zh: 分閫仗鉞者，固當以身先士卒為心，賊遺君父為恥。

translations.literal: Those who hold border command and wield the axe should by rights take leading the troops in person as their intent, and regard the enemy's leaving the sovereign and father as shame.
translations.idiomatic: Those who hold border command and wield the battle-axe should take leading the troops in person as their guiding principle and regard it as shameful when the enemy harms the sovereign and father of the realm.

sentences.zh: 而列城相望，堅壁自全，手握強兵，坐違成算，遂使腥膻得計，蛇豕肆行，焚劫我郡縣，係累我黎庶。

translations.literal: Yet walled cities face one another, holding firm behind walls to preserve themselves; with strong armies in hand they sit idle contrary to settled plans, so that barbarian stench gains its way, serpents and swine run riot, burning and plundering our prefectures and counties and binding and dragging off our common people.
translations.idiomatic: Yet walled cities stand face to face, each holding fast behind its walls to save itself. With strong armies in hand they sit idle against the settled plan, so that the barbarians gain their advantage, serpents and swine run wild, burn and plunder our prefectures and counties, and bind and drag off our people.

sentences.zh: 陛下攄人神之忿怒，憫河朔之生靈，爰御六師，親幸澶、魏，天聲一振，敵騎四逃，雖鎮、定道路已通，而德、棣烽塵未息，此殆將帥或未得人，邊奏或有壅閼，鄰境不相救援，糗糧須俟轉輸之所致也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has unleashed the wrath of men and gods and pitied the lives of the people north of the Yellow River; therefore you led the Six Armies and personally visited Cizhou and Weizhou. When Heaven's voice shook once, the enemy horsemen fled in four directions. Though roads to Zhenzhou and Dingzhou were already open, the beacon fires of Dezhou and Dizhou had not yet ceased—this is probably because generals may not have been the right men, border reports may have been blocked, neighboring territories did not rescue one another, and provisions had to await transport.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has unleashed the wrath of men and gods and pitied the people north of the Yellow River. You therefore led the Six Armies and personally visited Cizhou and Weizhou. When Heaven's voice shook once, the enemy horsemen fled in every direction. Though the roads to Zhenzhou and Dingzhou were already open, the beacon fires of Dezhou and Dizhou had not yet died down. This is probably because the generals were not the right men, border reports were blocked, neighboring territories failed to rescue one another, and provisions had to wait on transport.

sentences.zh: 將帥者何？

translations.literal: What of the generals?
translations.idiomatic: What of the generals?

sentences.zh: 或恃勇無謀，或忌功玩寇，但全城堡，不恤人民。

translations.literal: Some rely on courage without strategy; some envy merit and toy with the enemy, merely preserving castles and walls without caring for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Some rely on courage but lack strategy; some envy others' merit and play with the enemy, content merely to preserve their castles and walls while caring nothing for the people.

sentences.zh: 邊奏者何？

translations.literal: What of the border reports?
translations.idiomatic: What of the border reports?

sentences.zh: 護塞之臣，固祿守位，城池焚劫，不以實聞，老幼殺傷，託言他盜。

translations.literal: Border-defense officials, protecting their salaries and holding their posts, when cities and walls are burned and plundered do not report the truth; when old and young are killed and wounded, they claim other robbers did it.
translations.idiomatic: The officials who guard the frontier, protecting their salaries and clinging to their posts, do not report the truth when cities and walls are burned and plundered, and when old and young are killed and wounded they claim other bandits were responsible.

sentences.zh: 不救援者何？

translations.literal: What of those who do not rescue?
translations.idiomatic: What of those who fail to rescue?

sentences.zh: 緣邊州縣，城壘參錯，如輔車唇齒之相依，若頭目手足之相衛，託稱兵少不出，或待奏可乃行。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties along the border have interlocking fortifications, depending on one another like cheek and teeth in a carriage or head, eyes, hands, and feet guarding one another—they claim insufficient troops and do not go out, or wait for memorial approval before acting.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties along the border have interlocking fortifications, depending on one another like paired wheels or lip and teeth, guarding one another like head, eyes, hands, and feet. Yet they claim too few troops and refuse to go out, or wait for memorial approval before acting.

sentences.zh: 俟輦輸者何？

translations.literal: What of awaiting transport?
translations.idiomatic: What of waiting on transport?

sentences.zh: 敵騎往還，猋馳鳥逝，贏糧景從，萬兩方行，迨乎我來，寇已遁去。

translations.literal: Enemy horsemen come and go like storm winds—swift as birds vanishing; with grain carried on shoulder poles they must follow the sun's shadow, ten thousand taels of silver before they can move; by the time we arrive, the bandits have already fled.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy horsemen come and go like storm winds, swift as birds that vanish from sight. Provisions must be carried on shoulder poles and follow the sun's shadow; ten thousand taels of silver must be spent before a column can move. By the time we arrive, the raiders have already fled.

sentences.zh: 此四者，當今急務。

translations.literal: These four matters are urgent tasks of the present day.
translations.idiomatic: These four matters are the urgent tasks of the day.

sentences.zh: 擇將帥，則莫若文武之內，參用謀臣；

translations.literal: To select generals, nothing is better than combining strategic advisers from among civil and military officials;
translations.idiomatic: To choose generals, nothing is better than drawing strategic advisers from among both civil and military officials;

sentences.zh: 防壅閼，則莫若凡奏邊防，陛見庭問；

translations.literal: to prevent blocking, nothing is better than having all border-defense memorials presented at court for Your Majesty to question in the hall;
translations.idiomatic: to prevent obstruction, nothing is better than having every border memorial presented at court for Your Majesty to question in person;

sentences.zh: 合救援，則莫若督以軍令，聽其便宜；

translations.literal: to coordinate rescue, nothing is better than supervising with military orders and allowing discretionary action;
translations.idiomatic: to coordinate rescue, nothing is better than enforcing military orders while allowing discretionary action;

sentences.zh: 運糗糧，則莫若輕齎疾驅，角彼趫捷。

translations.literal: to transport provisions, nothing is better than carrying light loads and driving fast, matching their speed and agility.
translations.idiomatic: to move provisions, nothing is better than traveling light and driving hard, matching the enemy's speed and agility.

sentences.zh: 今大駕既駐鄴下，契丹終不敢萌心南牧，所慮薦食者，惟東北無備之城，繕完周防，不可不慎。

translations.literal: Now that the imperial carriage has encamped below Ye, the Khitan in the end dare not harbor thoughts of herding south; what is feared as devouring grain is only the unprepared cities of the northeast—repairing and fortifying them completely must not be treated lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the imperial carriage has encamped below Ye, the Khitan in the end dare not think of driving south to pasture their herds. What is feared as a devouring pest is only the unprepared cities of the northeast. Their repair and complete fortification must not be treated lightly.

sentences.zh: 且蜂蠆有毒，豺狼無厭。

translations.literal: Moreover, bees and scorpions have poison; wolves and jackals know no satiety.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, bees and scorpions carry poison, and wolves and jackals know no satiety.

sentences.zh: 今契丹西畏大兵，北無歸路，獸窮則搏，物不可輕，餘孽尚或稽誅，奔突亦宜預備。

translations.literal: Now the Khitan fear our great army to the west and have no road of return to the north—when beasts are cornered they fight; things must not be taken lightly. Remaining remnants may still delay execution, and sudden raids should also be prepared for in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Khitan fear our great army to the west and have no road of retreat to the north. When beasts are cornered they fight, and the enemy must not be taken lightly. Remaining remnants may still delay their destruction, and sudden raids should also be prepared for in advance.

sentences.zh: 大河津濟，處處有之，亦望量屯禁兵，扼其要害，則請和之使，不日可待。」

translations.literal: Fords across the Great River exist everywhere; it is also hoped that forbidden troops be stationed in appropriate numbers to hold the vital points—then envoys seeking peace may be awaited within days."
translations.idiomatic: Fords across the Great River exist everywhere. It is also hoped that imperial troops be stationed in appropriate numbers to hold the vital points. Then envoys seeking peace may be expected within days."

sentences.zh: 真宗覽而嘉之。

translations.literal: Zhenzong read it and commended it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong read it and commended it.

sentences.zh: 及傅潛逗撓無功，何又請斬潛以徇。

translations.literal: When Fu Qian dawdled and achieved nothing, He again requested that Qian be beheaded as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Qian dawdled and achieved nothing, Sun He again asked that Qian be executed as a public warning.

sentences.zh: 俄權戶部判官，出為京東轉運副使，又獻疏請擇州縣守宰，省三司冗員，遴選法官，增秩益奉。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Acting Adjudicator of the Ministry of Revenue, sent out as Vice Commissioner of the Eastern Capital Transport Circuit, and again submitted a memorial requesting selection of prefectural and county magistrates, reduction of redundant personnel in the Three Departments Office, careful selection of judicial officials, and increased rank and salary.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Acting Adjudicator of the Ministry of Revenue and sent out as Vice Commissioner of the Eastern Capital Transport Circuit. He again submitted a memorial asking that prefectural and county magistrates be carefully chosen, redundant personnel in the Three Departments Office be reduced, judicial officials be selected with care, and rank and salary be increased.

sentences.zh: 未幾，徙兩浙轉運使，加起居舍人。

translations.literal: Before long, he was transferred to Commissioner of the Two Zhe Transport Circuit and promoted to Diary Aide of the Sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Commissioner of the Two Zhe Transport Circuit and promoted to Diary Aide of the Sovereign.

sentences.zh: 景德初，代還，判太常禮院。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde, when his replacement arrived, he was made Administrator of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jingde (1004), when his replacement arrived, he was appointed Administrator of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Rites.

sentences.zh: 俄與晁迥、陳堯諮並命知制誥，賜金紫，掌三班院。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed together with Chao Hui and Chen Yaozī as Drafting Officer for the Secretariat, granted gold and purple robes, and put in charge of the Three-Rank Court.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed together with Chao Hui and Chen Yaozī as Drafting Officer for the Secretariat, granted gold and purple robes, and put in charge of the Three-Rank Court.

sentences.zh: 何先已被疾，勉強親職。

translations.literal: He had already been ill before this, yet forced himself to attend to his duties in person.
translations.idiomatic: He had already been ill, yet forced himself to attend to his duties in person.

sentences.zh: 一日，奏事上前，墜奏牘於地，俯而取之，復墜笏，有司劾以失儀，詔釋之。

translations.literal: One day, when presenting affairs before the throne, he dropped his memorial document to the ground; bowing to pick it up, he dropped his court tablet again. The responsible office impeached him for breach of ceremony; an edict released him.
translations.idiomatic: One day, while presenting affairs before the throne, he dropped his memorial to the ground; as he bowed to pick it up, he dropped his court tablet again. The responsible office impeached him for breach of ceremony, but an edict released him from punishment.

sentences.zh: 何慚，上章求改少卿監，分司西京養疾，上不許，第賜告，遣醫診視。

translations.literal: He was ashamed, submitted a memorial requesting transfer to a lesser directorate post with assignment to the Western Capital branch office to convalesce; the emperor did not permit it, but only granted leave and sent physicians to examine him.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, he submitted a memorial asking to be transferred to a lesser directorate post and assigned to the Western Capital branch office to convalesce. The emperor did not permit it, but only granted him leave and sent physicians to examine him.

sentences.zh: 醫勉其然艾，何答曰：「死生有命。」

translations.literal: The physicians urged him to submit to moxibustion; He replied: "Life and death are ordained by fate."
translations.idiomatic: The physicians urged him to submit to moxibustion. He replied, "Life and death are ordained by fate."

sentences.zh: 卒不聽。

translations.literal: In the end he did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he refused.

sentences.zh: 是冬卒，年四十四。

translations.literal: That winter he died, aged forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he died at the age of forty-four.

sentences.zh: 上在澶淵，聞之憫惜，錄其子言為大理評事。

translations.literal: The emperor was at Chanyuan; hearing of it he mourned and grieved, and enrolled his son Yan as investigating censor of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was at Chanyuan. When he heard the news he mourned and grieved, and enrolled Sun He's son Yan as investigating censor of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 何樂名教，勤接士類，後進之有詞藝者，必為稱揚。

translations.literal: He delighted in the fame of moral teaching, diligently received men of the scholar class, and for talented juniors in literary arts he always gave praise.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in the renown of moral teaching, diligently received men of the scholar class, and always spoke up for talented juniors in literary arts.

sentences.zh: 然性卞急，不能容物。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was harsh and impatient; he could not tolerate others.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his nature was harsh and impatient, and he could not tolerate others.

sentences.zh: 在浙右專務峻刻，州郡病焉。

translations.literal: In the Two Zhe region he devoted himself exclusively to severity; prefectures and counties suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: In the Two Zhe region he devoted himself exclusively to severity, and prefectures and counties suffered under it.

sentences.zh: 好學，著《駁史通》十餘篇，有集四十卷。

translations.literal: He loved learning and wrote more than ten chapters of Refuting the Comprehensive Mirror of History; he had a collected works of forty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and wrote more than ten chapters of Refuting the Comprehensive Mirror of History. He left a collected works of forty juan.

sentences.zh: 弟僅。

translations.literal: His younger brother was Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Jin.

sentences.zh: 弟 僅

translations.literal: Younger brother Jin
translations.idiomatic: Younger Brother Jin

sentences.zh: 僅，字鄰幾。

translations.literal: Jin, style name Linji.
translations.idiomatic: Jin, courtesy name Linji.

sentences.zh: 少勤學，與何俱有名於時。

translations.literal: In youth he studied diligently; he and He were both famed in their time.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied diligently, and he and Sun He were both famed in their time.

sentences.zh: 咸平元年，進士甲科，兄弟連冠貢籍，時人榮之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianping, he earned first rank in the jinshi examination; the brothers took top honors in succession in the examination rolls—a glory people of the time admired.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianping (998) he graduated in first rank on the jinshi examination; the brothers took top honors in succession on the examination rolls, a distinction people of the time admired.

sentences.zh: 解褐舒州團練推官，會詔舉賢良方正之士，趙安仁以僅名聞。

translations.literal: Upon doffing commoner's robes he was military prefectural adjutant of Shuzhou; when an edict summoned worthy and upright men, Zhao Anren reported Jin's name.
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering office he became military prefectural adjutant of Shuzhou. When an edict called for men of worth and integrity, Zhao Anren reported Jin's name.

sentences.zh: 策入第四等，擢光祿寺丞、直集賢院，俄知浚儀縣。

translations.literal: In the policy examination he entered the fourth grade and was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainment and straight official of the Hall of Assembled Worthies; soon he was made magistrate of Junyi County.
translations.idiomatic: In the policy examination he placed in the fourth grade and was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainment and straight official of the Hall of Assembled Worthies; soon afterward he was made magistrate of Junyi County.

sentences.zh: 景德初，拜太子中允、開封府推官，賜緋。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde, he was appointed Palace Secretariat Attendant and investigating magistrate of Kaifeng Prefecture, granted crimson robes.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jingde he was appointed Palace Secretariat Attendant and investigating magistrate of Kaifeng Prefecture, and was granted crimson robes.

sentences.zh: 北邊請盟，遣使交聘，僅首為國母生辰使。

translations.literal: When the northern border sought peace and envoys were exchanged, Jin was first sent as envoy for the birthday of the state mother.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern border sought peace and envoys were exchanged, Jin was first dispatched as envoy for the birthday of the state mother.

sentences.zh: 改本府判官，遷右正言、知制誥，賜金紫，同知審官院。

translations.literal: He was changed to investigating magistrate of the prefecture, promoted to Right Remonstrance Officer and Drafting Officer for the Secretariat, granted gold and purple robes, and jointly made Administrator of the Bureau of Official Evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to investigating magistrate of the prefecture, promoted to Right Remonstrance Officer and Drafting Officer for the Secretariat, granted gold and purple robes, and jointly appointed Administrator of the Bureau of Official Evaluation.

sentences.zh: 是冬，永興孫全照求代，真宗思擇循良任之，御書邊肅洎僅二名示宰相。

translations.literal: That winter, Sun Quanzhao of Yongxing requested replacement; Zhenzong thought to select a virtuous and capable man—he personally wrote the two names Bian Su and Jin for the chief councilors.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Sun Quanzhao of Yongxing requested a replacement. Zhenzong wished to choose a virtuous and capable man and personally wrote the two names Bian Su and Jin for the chief councilors.

sentences.zh: 或言僅嘗倅京府，諳民政，乃命知永興軍府。

translations.literal: Some said Jin had once served as vice magistrate of the capital prefecture and knew civil administration; he was therefore appointed military prefect of Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: Some said Jin had once served as vice magistrate of the capital prefecture and understood civil administration, so he was appointed military prefect of Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 僅純厚長者，為政頗寬，嘗詔戒焉。

translations.literal: Jin was simple, generous, and a man of mature years; in governance he was quite lenient and was once admonished by edict.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was simple, generous, and a man of mature years. In governance he was quite lenient and was once admonished by edict.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符元年，加比部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu, he was promoted to Vice Director of the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu (1008) he was promoted to Vice Director of the Revenue Section.

sentences.zh: 代還，知審刑院。

translations.literal: When his replacement arrived, he was made Administrator of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When his replacement arrived, he was appointed Administrator of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 頃之，拜右諫議大夫、集賢院學士、權知開封府。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Right Remonstrance Censor, Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and Acting Administrator of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Right Remonstrance Censor, Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and Acting Administrator of Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 改左諫議大夫，出知河中府。

translations.literal: He was changed to Left Remonstrance Censor and sent out as prefect of Hezhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Left Remonstrance Censor and sent out as prefect of Hezhong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歸朝，復領審刑院。

translations.literal: Upon returning to court, he again headed the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Upon returning to court, he again headed the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 久次，進給事中。

translations.literal: After long waiting in rank, he was promoted to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: After long waiting in rank, he was promoted to Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 天禧元年正月卒，年四十九。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Tianxi, he died, aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Tianxi (1017) he died at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 錄其子大理評事和為衛尉寺丞。

translations.literal: His son He, investigating censor of the Court of Judicial Review, was enrolled as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son He, investigating censor of the Court of Judicial Review, was enrolled as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 僅性端愨，中立無競，篤於儒學，士大夫推其履尚，有集五十卷。

translations.literal: Jin's nature was upright and honest, neutral without contention, devoted to Confucian learning; scholar-officials praised his conduct, and he had a collected works of fifty juan.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's nature was upright and honest, neutral and uncontentious, and devoted to Confucian learning. Scholar-officials praised his conduct, and he left a collected works of fifty juan.

sentences.zh: 僅弟侑，亦登進士第，至殿中丞。

translations.literal: Jin's younger brother You also passed the jinshi examination, reaching Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's younger brother You also passed the jinshi examination and rose to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 朱台符

translations.literal: Zhu Taifu
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Taifu

sentences.zh: 朱台符，字拱正，眉州眉山人。

translations.literal: Zhu Taifu, style name Gongzheng, was a man of Meishan in Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Taifu, courtesy name Gongzheng, was a native of Meishan in Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 父賦，舉拔萃，歷度支判官，卒於殿中丞。

translations.literal: His father Fu passed the specially elevated examination, served as fiscal affairs adjudicator, and died while Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fu passed the specially elevated examination, served as fiscal affairs adjudicator, and died while holding the post of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 台符少聰穎，十歲能屬辭，嘗作《黃山樓記》，士友稱之。

translations.literal: Taifu was clever and quick from youth; at ten he could compose prose and once wrote "Record of Huangshan Tower," which friends praised.
translations.idiomatic: Taifu was clever and quick from youth. At ten he could compose prose and once wrote "Record of Huangshan Tower," which his friends praised.

sentences.zh: 及長，善詞賦。

translations.literal: When grown, he was skilled at lyric prose and rhapsodies.
translations.idiomatic: When grown, he was skilled at lyric prose and rhapsodies.

sentences.zh: 時太宗廷試貢士，多擢敏速者，台符與同輩課試，以尺晷成一賦。

translations.literal: At that time when Taizong held palace examinations for presented scholars, he often promoted those who were quick and nimble; Taifu competed in tests with contemporaries, completing a rhapsody within the span of a foot-measure sundial.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, when Emperor Taizong held palace examinations for presented scholars, he often favored those who were quick and nimble. Taifu competed in tests with his contemporaries and completed a rhapsody within the span of a foot-measure sundial.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年，進士登甲科，解褐將作監丞、通判青州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunhua, he passed the jinshi examination in first rank, and upon doffing commoner's robes was appointed Assistant Director of the Directorate of Works and Vice Administrator of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chunhua (990) he passed the jinshi examination in first rank and, upon entering office, was appointed Assistant Director of the Directorate of Works and Vice Administrator of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 召入直史館，賜緋魚，再遷秘書丞、知浚儀縣。

translations.literal: He was summoned to serve in the Historiography Institute, granted crimson fish, and again promoted to Secretary of the Palace Library and magistrate of Junyi County.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the Historiography Institute, granted the crimson fish badge, and again promoted to Secretary of the Palace Library and magistrate of Junyi County.

sentences.zh: 咸平元年，與楊礪、李若拙、梁顥同知貢舉，俄以京府舊僚，擢太常博士，出為京西轉運副使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianping, together with Yang Li, Li Ruozhuo, and Liang Hao he administered the examination for presented scholars; soon, as a former colleague of the capital prefecture, he was promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and sent out as Vice Commissioner of the Western Capital Transport Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianping (998), together with Yang Li, Li Ruozhuo, and Liang Hao, he administered the examination for presented scholars. Soon afterward, as a former colleague in the capital prefecture, he was promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and sent out as Vice Commissioner of the Western Capital Transport Circuit.

sentences.zh: 時北邊為梗，台符上言曰：

translations.literal: At the time the northern border was obstructed; Taifu submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: At the time the northern border was troubled. Taifu submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 「臣聞蠻夷猾夏，《帝典》所載，商、周而下，數為邊害。

translations.literal: "I have heard that barbarians plague China—this is recorded in the Canon of Emperor Yao; from Shang and Zhou downward, they repeatedly became border calamities.
translations.idiomatic: "I have heard that when barbarians plague China, it is recorded in the Canon of Emperor Yao. From Shang and Zhou downward, they have repeatedly become a scourge on the borders.

sentences.zh: 或振旅薄伐，或和親修好，歷代經營，斯為良策。

translations.literal: Sometimes one rouses the army for a punitive expedition; sometimes one seals marriage alliances and renews friendly ties—generations have managed affairs thus; this is the sound policy.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes you march in force to chastise the foe; sometimes you bind peace through marriage and diplomacy. That is how successive dynasties have managed the frontier—and it remains the wise course.

sentences.zh: 至於秦築長城而黔首叛，漢絕大漠而海內虛，逞志一時，貽笑萬代，此商鑒不遠也。

translations.literal: As for Qin building the Long Wall and the black-headed masses rebelling, Han cutting off beyond the great desert and the realm within the seas becoming empty—indulging ambition for a moment, leaving laughter for ten thousand generations—this mirror of Shang is not far off.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin raised the Great Wall, the people rose against it; when Han pushed deep into the desert, the heartland was drained empty. Ambition satisfied for a season became mockery for all posterity—the lesson of the Shang is still close at hand.

sentences.zh: 頃者，晉氏失御，中原亂離，太祖深鑒往古，酌取中道，與民休息，遣使往來。

translations.literal: Recently the house of Jin lost control; the Central Plain was chaotic and torn apart. Taizu deeply took past ages as mirror, weighed and took the middle way, gave the people rest, and sent envoys back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago the Jin lost the throne and the Central Plain fell into chaos. Our Taizu studied the past, chose a measured path, let the people recover, and kept diplomatic contact with the border peoples.

sentences.zh: 二十年間，罕聞入寇，大省戍邊之卒，不興出塞之兵。

translations.literal: Within twenty years, one rarely heard of incursions; frontier garrison troops were greatly reduced, and armies beyond the passes were not raised.
translations.idiomatic: For twenty years border raids were seldom heard of. Garrisons were sharply cut, and no campaigns were launched beyond the frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 關防謐寧，府庫充溢，信深得制禦之道也。
