translations.literal: Passes and defenses were tranquil and secure; treasuries were full and overflowing—truly he deeply attained the way of controlling and defending.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier stayed quiet, the coffers swelled—clear proof that he had mastered the art of defense without overreach.

sentences.zh: 幽薊之地，實維我疆，尚隔混同，所宜開拓。

translations.literal: The lands of You and Ji are truly our territory, yet they still lie beyond the Hun Tong River—it is fitting to open and expand them.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou and Jizhou are rightfully ours, yet remain cut off by the Hun Tong River; they ought to be recovered and developed.

sentences.zh: 太宗平晉之後，因其兵勢，將遂取之。

translations.literal: After Taizong pacified Jin, relying on his military momentum, he was about to take it as well.
translations.idiomatic: Once Taizong had subdued Jin, he meant to press that military advantage and seize the region outright.

sentences.zh: 人雖協謀，天未厭亂，螗斧拒轍，用稽靈誅。

translations.literal: Though men coordinated their plans, Heaven had not yet tired of chaos; like mantis and axe against the wheel track, they thereby incurred Heaven's punitive strike.
translations.idiomatic: Men may plot together, but Heaven had not finished with disorder. They resisted like a mantis raising its arms against a chariot wheel—and brought divine retribution down upon themselves.

sentences.zh: 重興吊伐之師，又作遷延之役。

translations.literal: Again he raised armies on punitive expedition, and again engaged in protracted campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Once more he sent punitive armies across the border—and once more sank into grinding, drawn-out war.

sentences.zh: 自茲厥後，大肆凶鋒，殺略軍民，攻拔城砦，長驅深入，莫可禁止。

translations.literal: From that time onward they greatly unleashed ferocious blades, killed and plundered soldiers and civilians, attacked and captured walled cities and stockades, drove deep in long charges—nothing could stop them.
translations.idiomatic: After that the enemy savagely rampaged—slaughtering and looting troops and civilians, storming towns and forts, and riding deep into our territory with no one able to halt them.

sentences.zh: 當是時也，以河為塞，而趙、魏之間，幾非國家所有。

translations.literal: At that time, with the Yellow River as the barrier, the region between Zhao and Wei was almost no longer held by the state.
translations.idiomatic: In those days the Yellow River served as our line of defense, and the lands between Zhao and Wei were nearly lost to the realm.

sentences.zh: 既阻歡盟，乃為備禦，屯士馬，益將帥，芻粟之飛輓，金帛之委輸，贍給賞賜，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Once friendly alliance was blocked, defensive preparations were made—soldiers and horses were stationed, generals and commanders were increased; fodder and grain flew in transport, gold and silk were continuously conveyed; provisions, rewards, and bestowals were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: When amity failed, we turned to defense—massing troops and appointing more commanders, rushing fodder and grain northward, pouring out gold and silk in pay and reward, in sums beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 繇是國家之食貨，匱於河朔矣。

translations.literal: Hence the state's food and goods were depleted in the Hebei region.
translations.idiomatic: From this the state's grain and wealth were exhausted in the north.

sentences.zh: 陛下自天受命，與物更始，繼遷授節，黎桓加爵，咸命使者鎮撫其邦。

translations.literal: Your Majesty received the mandate from Heaven and began anew with all things; Li Jiqian was granted insignia, Le Huan was ennobled—all were ordered envoys to pacify and soothe their domains.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty ascended by Heaven's mandate and renewed the realm, Li Jiqian has been invested with command, Le Huan ennobled, and envoys dispatched to reassure both their peoples.

sentences.zh: 惟彼契丹，未加渥澤，非所以柔遠能邇，昭王道之無偏也。

translations.literal: Only toward the Khitan was generous favor not extended—not the way to soften the distant and cherish the near, to manifest the King's Way without partiality.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Khitan alone have received no comparable grace—hardly the way to win over distant peoples, reassure those nearby, and show that the royal way knows no favoritism.

sentences.zh: 今祥禫將終，中外引頸觀聽德音。

translations.literal: Now the xiang and chan mourning periods are about to end; within and without the court all stretch their necks, watching and listening for words of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Your mourning period is nearing its end, and court and country alike await the gracious pronouncement you will soon issue.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為宜於此時赦契丹罪，擇文武才略習知邊境辨說之士，為一介使，以嗣位服除，修好鄰國，往告諭之。

translations.literal: This foolish subject thinks that at this time one should pardon the Khitan's offenses, select men of civil and military talent and strategy familiar with the borders and skilled in persuasion to serve as envoys—on the occasion of succession to the throne and completion of mourning—to renew friendship with neighboring states and go to announce and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly suggest that now is the moment to pardon the Khitan, choose able civil and military men who know the frontier and can speak persuasively, and send them as envoys—marking your accession and the end of mourning—to restore good relations and explain your intent.

sentences.zh: 彼十年以來，不復犯塞，以臣計之，力有不足，志欲歸向，而未得其間也。

translations.literal: They have not again violated the border for ten years; by my reckoning their strength is insufficient, their intent wishes to turn toward us, yet they have not yet found the opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: For ten years they have not raided our borders. In my judgment their power is limited and their hearts incline toward us—they simply lack an opening.

sentences.zh: 今若垂天覆之仁，假來王之便，必歡悅慕義，遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: If now you extend heaven-covering benevolence and grant the convenience of coming to court, they will surely rejoice, admire righteousness, and send envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: If you now shower them with encompassing mercy and make it easy for them to come to court, they will gladly embrace our righteousness and send tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 因與之盡捐前惡，復尋舊盟，利以貨財，許以關市，如太祖故事，使之懷恩畏威。

translations.literal: Then with them utterly abandon past enmities, seek again the old alliance, benefit them with goods and wealth, permit border markets—as in Taizu's precedent—causing them to cherish gratitude and fear authority.
translations.idiomatic: Then let us set aside old grievances, renew the former pact, offer trade in goods and open border markets as Taizu once did—so that they feel both gratitude and awe.

sentences.zh: 則兩國既和，無北顧之憂，可以專力西鄙，繼遷自當革心而束手矣，是一舉而兩得也。」

translations.literal: Then the two states being at peace, with no worry of looking north, one can concentrate force on the western frontier; Li Jiqian will naturally reform his heart and bind his hands—it is one act gaining two gains."
translations.idiomatic: With peace in the north, we need no longer glance over our shoulder; we can devote our strength to the west, and Li Jiqian will surely submit of his own accord. One stroke, two gains."

sentences.zh: 台符又自請往使，時論韙之。

translations.literal: Taifu again volunteered to go as envoy; contemporary opinion approved him.
translations.idiomatic: Taifu then offered to go as envoy himself, and public opinion applauded the proposal.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年春，旱，詔求直言。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year of Xianping there was drought; an edict sought forthright speech.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Xianping 2, drought struck and the throne called for candid memorials.

sentences.zh: 台符上疏，請重農積穀，任將選兵，慎擇守令，考課黜陟，輕徭節用，均賦慎刑，責任大臣，與圖治道。

translations.literal: Taifu submitted a memorial asking to emphasize agriculture and store grain, appoint generals and select troops, carefully choose prefects and magistrates, examine performance for promotion and dismissal, lighten corvée and economize expenditure, equalize levies and be careful in punishments, entrust responsibility to great ministers, and together plan the way of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Taifu memorialized urging heavier emphasis on farming and grain reserves, better generals and sharper troops, careful selection of local officials, merit-based promotion and removal, lighter burdens and tighter spending, fairer taxes and more cautious justice, greater accountability for senior ministers, and a shared program of good government.

sentences.zh: 奏入，優詔褒答。

translations.literal: The memorial entered; a favorable edict praised and replied.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the Emperor answered with a warm edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 入為鹽鐵判官，改判戶部勾院，拜工部員外郎，換度支判官。

translations.literal: He entered service as Salt and Iron Commissioner; changed to serve as Commissioner of the Household Department Checking Office; was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Works; and transferred to Expenditure Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Salt and Iron Commissioner, then Household Accounts Commissioner, promoted to Vice Director of Works, and reassigned as Expenditure Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 景德初，鄭文寶為陝西轉運，或言其張皇生事，徙台符代之，仍賜金紫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde, Zheng Wenbao was Shaanxi transport commissioner; some said he exaggerated affairs and stirred trouble—Taifu was moved to replace him, and still granted gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingde, Zheng Wenbao served as Shaanxi transport commissioner until critics accused him of alarmism and needless provocation. Taifu replaced him and was awarded the gold seal and purple robe.

sentences.zh: 台符俊爽好謀，然頗以刻碎為舉職。

translations.literal: Taifu was sharp and open, fond of scheming, yet took petty meticulousness as fulfilling his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Taifu was brilliant and resourceful, but he tended to equate fussy nitpicking with conscientious service.

sentences.zh: 與楊覃聯事，覃頗欲因仍舊貫，台符則更革煩擾，議事違戾，交相掎奏，以不協聞，命御史視其狀。

translations.literal: He jointly handled affairs with Yang Tan; Tan quite wished to follow old practices, while Taifu reformed with vexing changes. In deliberating affairs they clashed, mutually submitted impeachments, were reported as out of harmony, and a censor was ordered to investigate the case.
translations.idiomatic: Serving alongside Yang Tan, he found Tan inclined to leave things as they were while he pushed disruptive reforms. Their disputes escalated into mutual impeachments; when word reached the throne that they could not work together, a censor was sent to review the affair.

sentences.zh: 九月，徙台符知郢州，覃知隨州。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Taifu was moved to prefect of E Prefecture, and Tan to prefect of Sui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Taifu was reassigned as prefect of Ezhou and Tan as prefect of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，召還，會執政有不喜者，復出知洪州，卒於舟次，年四十二。

translations.literal: In the third year he was recalled; chancing upon someone in power who disliked him, he was again sent out as prefect of Hong Prefecture; he died aboard ship at age forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was recalled, but an unfriendly member of the chief council blocked him and he was sent out again as prefect of Hongzhou. He died on the river at forty-two.

sentences.zh: 賜其子公佐同學究出身，賵錢二十萬。

translations.literal: His son Gongzuo was granted the status of a fellow classics scholar, and funeral gift money of two hundred thousand was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gongzuo was granted the rank of fellow classics scholar, and two hundred thousand cash in funeral gifts was awarded.

sentences.zh: 台符好學，敏於屬辭，喜延譽後進，有集三十卷。

translations.literal: Taifu loved learning, was quick at composing prose, delighted in extending fame to juniors, and had a collected works of thirty juan.
translations.idiomatic: Taifu was a devoted scholar, fluent with the pen, generous in promoting younger men, and left a collected works in thirty juan.

sentences.zh: 公佐及台符弟昌符，大中祥符中，舉進士，廷試並得第五人。

translations.literal: Gongzuo and Taifu's younger brother Changfu, in the Dazhong Xiangfu era, passed the jinshi examination; in the palace examination both placed fifth.
translations.idiomatic: During Dazhong Xiangfu, Gongzuo and Taifu's brother Changfu both passed the jinshi examination and ranked fifth in the palace test.

sentences.zh: 初，昌符登科，宰相言昌符即台符弟，上因言台符有文學及著述可采，甚嗟悼之。

translations.literal: Initially, when Changfu passed the examination, the chief councilor said Changfu was Taifu's younger brother; the Emperor then spoke of Taifu's literary learning and writings worth collecting, and deeply sighed in grief.
translations.idiomatic: When Changfu first passed the exams, the chief councilor noted that he was Taifu's brother. The Emperor then recalled Taifu's literary gifts and the writings worth preserving, and mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 公佐卒，又以次子壽隆試將作監主簿。

translations.literal: When Gongzuo died, his second son Shoulong was tested and appointed Master of Records in the Directorate of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After Gongzuo's death, his second son Shoulong was examined and appointed master of records in the Directorate of Works.

sentences.zh: 昌符為屯田員外郎。

translations.literal: Changfu served as Vice Director in the Ministry of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: Changfu became Vice Director of the Ministry of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 戚綸，字仲言，應天楚丘人。

translations.literal: Qi Lun, style name Zhongyan, was a man of Chuqiu in Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Lun, courtesy name Zhongyan, was a native of Chuqiu in Yingtian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父同文，字文約，自有傳。

translations.literal: Qi Tongwen, style name Wenyu, has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His kinsman Qi Tongwen, courtesy name Wenyu, has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 綸少與兄維以文行知名，篤於古學，喜談名教。

translations.literal: Lun in youth, together with his elder brother Wei, was known for literary conduct; he was devoted to ancient learning and fond of discussing name and teaching.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Lun and his elder brother Wei were known for learning and integrity. He was steeped in classical studies and loved to discourse on moral principle.

sentences.zh: 太平興國八年，舉進士，解褐沂水主簿。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo he passed the jinshi examination; upon leaving coarse cloth he took post as chief clerk of Yishui.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 8 he passed the jinshi and, on first entering office, became chief clerk of Yishui.

sentences.zh: 按版籍，得逋戶脫口漏租者甚眾。

translations.literal: Examining the registers, he found many absconding households who had slipped through and omitted rent.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing the tax rolls, he uncovered a great many hidden households that had evaded registration and rent.

sentences.zh: 徙知太和縣。

translations.literal: He was moved to serve as magistrate of Taihe County.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as magistrate of Taihe County.

sentences.zh: 同文卒於隨州，綸徒步奔訃千里餘。

translations.literal: Tongwen died in Sui Prefecture; Lun went on foot to rush the news of death over a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: When Tongwen died in Suizhou, Lun walked more than a thousand li to bring home word of his death.

sentences.zh: 俄詔起復蒞職，就加大理評事。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to leave mourning and resume office; he was concurrently promoted to Reviewing Officer of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was ordered to leave mourning and return to duty, and was promoted to reviewing officer of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 江外民險悍多構訟，為《諭民詩》五十篇，因時俗耳目之事，以申規誨，老幼多傳誦之。

translations.literal: The people beyond the river were fierce and litigious; he wrote fifty "Poems to Instruct the People," using matters before the eyes of popular custom to set forth admonition—old and young widely recited them.
translations.idiomatic: The folk south of the Yangzi were truculent and lawsuit-prone. He composed fifty "Poems to Instruct the People," drawing on everyday scenes to teach right conduct, and young and old alike memorized them.

sentences.zh: 每歲時必與獄囚約，遣歸祀其先，皆如期而還。

translations.literal: Every year at the seasons he would make agreements with prison inmates, release them to return and sacrifice to their ancestors—all returned on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Each year at the festivals he would parole prisoners on their word to go home and honor their ancestors—and every one returned on time.

sentences.zh: 遷光祿丞，坐鞫獄陳州失實，免官。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; convicted for investigating a case in Chen Prefecture with false findings, he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, he was later stripped of office for mishandling a trial in Chenzhou with findings that did not match the facts.

sentences.zh: 著《理道評》十二篇，錢若水、王禹偁深所賞重。

translations.literal: He authored twelve chapters of "Assessments on the Way of Governance"; Qian Ruoshui and Wang Yucheng deeply valued them.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote twelve essays entitled Assessments on the Way of Governance, which Qian Ruoshui and Wang Yucheng held in the highest regard.

sentences.zh: 久之，復授大理評事、知永嘉縣，境有陂塘之利，浚治以備水旱。

translations.literal: After a long while he was again appointed Reviewing Officer and magistrate of Yongjia County; the district had the benefit of ponds and dikes—he dredged and managed them against flood and drought.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was restored as reviewing officer and magistrate of Yongjia. Where the county enjoyed pond and dyke works, he dredged and maintained them against flood and drought.

sentences.zh: 復為光祿寺丞，轉運使又上其政績，連詔褒之。

translations.literal: Again he served as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; the transport commissioner again reported his administrative achievements, and successive edicts praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; the transport commissioner once more commended his record, and the throne answered with repeated praise.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，轉著作佐郎、通判泰州。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong acceded, he was transferred to Assistant Compiler and vice-prefect of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong came to the throne, Lun was made assistant compiler and vice-prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 將行，秘書監楊徽之薦其文學純謹，宜在館閣，命為秘閣校理。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, Supervising Secretary Yang Huizhi recommended his literary learning as pure and careful, suitable for the archive halls—he was ordered collator of the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could leave, Supervising Secretary Yang Huizhi praised his refined and conscientious scholarship and urged that he belong in the palace archives. He was appointed collator of the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 受詔考校司天臺職官，定州縣職田條制。

translations.literal: He received an edict to examine and review Bureau of Astronomy officials and fix regulations for prefectural and county official fields.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to review the staff of the Bureau of Astronomy and to draft rules governing official fields in prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 詔館閣官以舊文獻，上嘉綸所著，特改太常丞，俄判鼓司、登聞院。

translations.literal: An edict ordered archive officials to submit old documents; the Emperor praised Lun's writings, specially changed him to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and soon had him judge the Drum Office and Petition Office.
translations.idiomatic: When archive officials were commanded to submit historical materials, the Emperor admired Lun's work, promoted him to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and soon put him in charge of the Drum Office and Petition Office.

sentences.zh: 出內府緡帛市邊糧，詔綸乘傳往均市之。

translations.literal: Inner-treasury silk and cash were issued to purchase frontier grain; an edict ordered Lun to travel by post horse to equalize the market purchases.
translations.idiomatic: Silk and cash from the inner treasury were released to buy frontier grain, and Lun was ordered to ride post horses north to oversee fair purchasing.

sentences.zh: 景德元年，判三司開拆，賜緋魚，改鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingde he judged the Three Departments Opening and Checking Office, was granted red fish insignia, and was changed to Salt and Iron Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde 1 he served as judge of the Three Departments Opening and Checking Office, received the red fish badge, and was reassigned as Salt and Iron Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 上疏言邊事，甚被嘉獎。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial on border affairs and was greatly rewarded with praise.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on frontier policy and won high praise from the throne.

sentences.zh: 十月，拜右正言、龍圖閣待制，賜金紫。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was appointed Right Remonstrator and Hanlin Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, and granted gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was made Right Remonstrator and Dragon Diagram Hall academician, and awarded the gold seal and purple robe.

sentences.zh: 時初建是職，與杜鎬並命，人皆榮之。

translations.literal: At that time this post was newly established; appointed together with Du Hao, everyone considered it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: The post had only just been created; appointed alongside Du Hao, both men were envied throughout the court.

sentences.zh: 綸久次州縣，留意吏事，每便殿請對，語必移晷，或夜中召見，多所敷啟。

translations.literal: Lun had long served in prefectures and counties and was attentive to administrative affairs; each time he requested audience in the informal hall, conversation always extended past the gnomon shadow; sometimes he was summoned at night, and many matters were submitted and opened.
translations.idiomatic: Long seasoned in local office, Lun knew the nuts and bolts of administration. At informal audiences his talks ran past the hour; sometimes the Emperor summoned him at night, and he laid out issue after issue.

sentences.zh: 俄上奏曰：「夫出納獻替，王臣之任；

translations.literal: Soon he submitted a memorial saying: Disbursement and receipt, offering and replacement—the charge of a king's minister;
translations.idiomatic: Soon he memorialized: To receive and disburse, to advise and to withdraw—such is a minister's duty;

sentences.zh: 章疏奏議，諫者之職。

translations.literal: memorials, submissions, and remonstrances—the duty of the remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: memorials and remonstrance—the remonstrator's charge.

sentences.zh: 臣屢蒙召對，皆延數刻，屈萬乘之尊，接一介之士，聖德淵深，包納荒穢，體其至愚，不罪觸犯，安敢循嘿不言。

translations.literal: Your subject has repeatedly been granted audience, each time extended several quarters of an hour; bending the dignity of ten thousand chariots to receive a single petty officer—the sage virtue is profound and deep, embracing even the crude and foul, understanding my utmost foolishness and not punishing offense—how dare I follow silence and not speak?
translations.idiomatic: I have been summoned again and again, each audience lasting long into the watch. Your Majesty, lord of ten thousand chariots, has stooped to hear one low officer; your virtue is boundless, tolerating even my coarse speech and never punishing my bluntness. How then can I remain silent?

sentences.zh: 謹摭十事該治本者附於章左：一曰王畿關輔，二曰五等封建，三曰復制科，四曰崇國學，五曰辟曠土，六曰修貢舉，七曰任大臣，八曰置平糴，九曰益廂軍、減禁兵，十曰修《六典》令式。」

translations.literal: Respectfully selecting ten matters bearing on root governance to attach at the memorial's left: first, the capital region and pass auxiliaries; second, five ranks of enfeoffment; third, restore special examination categories; fourth, exalt the National University; fifth, open wasteland; sixth, repair tribute and examination; seventh, entrust great ministers; eighth, establish fair-price grain purchase; ninth, increase corvée soldiers and reduce palace guards; tenth, compile the Six Canon regulations.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully set down ten reforms touching the foundations of rule: (1) the capital and its heartland defenses; (2) graded enfeoffment; (3) revival of special examination tracks; (4) strengthening the National University; (5) opening idle land; (6) reform of the civil service exams; (7) greater reliance on senior ministers; (8) establishment of fair-price granaries; (9) expanding the corvée army while trimming the palace guard; (10) codification of the Six Canon regulations.

sentences.zh: 詞頗深切，上為嘉獎。

translations.literal: The language was quite earnest; the Emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The wording was deeply felt, and the Emperor commended him.

sentences.zh: 二年，與趙安仁、晁迥、陳充、朱巽同知貢舉，綸上言取士之法，多所規制，並納用焉。

translations.literal: In the second year, together with Zhao Anren, Chao Jiong, Chen Chong, and Zhu Yi he served as co-examiners for the tribute examination; Lun submitted on methods of selecting scholars—many regulations, all adopted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he served with Zhao Anren, Chao Jiong, Chen Chong, and Zhu Yi as chief examiners. Lun proposed reforms to the selection of scholars; many were adopted.

sentences.zh: 預修《冊府元龜》，會置官總在京諸司之務，凡百三十司，命綸與劉承珪同領其事。

translations.literal: He participated in compiling the Prime Tortoise of the Imperial Archive; when offices were established to oversee all capital bureaus—one hundred and thirty in all—Lun and Liu Chenggui were ordered jointly to head the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He helped compile the Prime Tortoise of the Imperial Archive. When a new office was created to supervise the capital's 130 bureaus, Lun and Liu Chenggui were appointed to lead it together.

sentences.zh: 判鴻臚寺。

translations.literal: He judged the Court of State Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief administrator of the Court of State Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 先是，群臣詔葬，公私所費無定式。

translations.literal: Before this, when ministers were buried by imperial edict, public and private expenses had no fixed pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when officials were buried by imperial decree, there was no fixed standard for public or private costs.

sentences.zh: 綸言其事，詔同晁迥、朱巽、劉承珪校品秩之差，定為制度，遂遵行之。

translations.literal: Lun spoke on the matter; an edict ordered him together with Chao Jiong, Zhu Yi, and Liu Chenggui to compare rank differences, fix regulations, and then they were followed in practice.
translations.idiomatic: Lun raised the issue, and the throne ordered him, Chao Jiong, Zhu Yi, and Liu Chenggui to grade expenses by rank and codify the rules, which thereafter became standard.

sentences.zh: 綸以三公、尚書、九列之任，唐末以來，有司漸繁，綱目不一，謂宜采《通禮》、《六典》令式，比類沿革，著為大典，時論稱之。

translations.literal: Lun held that the posts of the Three Excellencies, Ministers, and Nine Ranks—since late Tang the bureaus had gradually multiplied and categories were not unified—and thought one should gather the Comprehensive Rites and Six Canon regulations, compare types and trace changes, and compile a great canon; contemporary opinion praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Lun argued that since late Tang the offices of the Three Excellencies, ministers, and department heads had proliferated without consistent organization. He urged drawing on the Comprehensive Rites and Six Canon to harmonize precedent into a grand code—a proposal widely applauded.

sentences.zh: 進秩右司諫、兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: He advanced in rank to Right Remonstrator of the Secretariat and Vice Director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Remonstrator of the Secretariat and Vice Director of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 時詔禁群臣匿名上封及非次升殿奏事，綸謂：「忠讜之入，當開獎言路，若疏遠之士，尤艱請對。」

translations.literal: At the time an edict forbade ministers' anonymous sealed memorials and irregular ascending the hall to report affairs; Lun said: When loyal straightforward speech enters, one should open and encourage the path of speech; for men remote and distant, requesting audience is especially difficult.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne forbade anonymous memorials and unscheduled appearances in court, Lun replied: If loyal counsel is to reach you, the channels of speech must be kept open—especially for men far from power, for whom an audience is already hard to obtain.

sentences.zh: 上頗嘉之。

translations.literal: The Emperor rather praised this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was much pleased.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符元年，掌吏部選事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu he managed Ministry of Personnel selection affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong Xiangfu 1 he took charge of appointments in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 上初受靈文，綸上疏曰：「臣遐稽載籍，歷考秘文，驗靈應之垂祥，顧天人之相接。

translations.literal: When the Emperor first received the spirit text, Lun submitted a memorial saying: Your subject from afar traced the records, exhaustively examined secret texts, verified spiritual responses descending as auspice, and contemplated heaven and human in mutual contact.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor first received the heavenly text, Lun memorialized: I have searched the archives and examined the secret writings, confirming that divine responses foretell blessing and that Heaven and humanity meet in one design.

sentences.zh: 陛下紹二聖丕業，啟萬世鴻基，勤行企道，恭默思元，上天降鑒，瑞牒昭錫，聿示臨民之戒，用恢奕葉之祥。

translations.literal: Your Majesty continues the great enterprise of the two sages, opens a ten-thousand-year grand foundation, diligently practices aspiring to the Way, reverently silent pondering the Origin; Heaven above descends inspection, auspicious documents are brightly bestowed, thereby showing the warning of governing the people, to expand the fortune of glorious generations.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty inherits the great work of the two previous emperors and lays a foundation for ages to come—earnest in virtue, reverent before the Way. Heaven has shown its approval, bestowing auspicious writs as both warning in rule and blessing for generations yet unborn.

sentences.zh: 乞詔有司，速修大祀，載命侍從，摹寫祥符，勒於嘉玉，藏之太廟，別以副本秘於中禁，傳示萬葉，無敢怠荒。

translations.literal: I beg edict to the responsible offices to swiftly repair the great sacrifice, charge attendant officials to copy the auspicious symbols, inscribe them on fine jade, store them in the Grand Temple, separately seal a copy in the inner forbidden precinct, and transmit them to ten thousand generations—none dare slacken in neglect.
translations.idiomatic: I pray that responsible offices be ordered at once to prepare the great rites, that attendant officials copy the sacred signs, carve them on fine jade, deposit them in the Grand Temple, keep a duplicate sealed within the inner palace, and pass them down through the ages without lapse.

sentences.zh: 然臣恐流俗幻惑狂謀，以人鬼之妖辭，亂天書之真旨。

translations.literal: Yet your subject fears popular fads, delusions, and wild schemes—using demonic words of men and ghosts to confuse the true purport of Heaven's book.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I fear that vulgar superstition and reckless invention will twist human and ghostly fantasies into a corruption of Heaven's true message.

sentences.zh: 伏望端守元符，凝神正道，以答天貺，以惠烝黎。」

translations.literal: I humbly hope you will uprightly guard the primal tally, concentrate spirit on the correct Way, to answer Heaven's gift and benefit the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to hold fast to the sacred token, fix your mind on the right path, answer Heaven's grace, and bring benefit to the people.

sentences.zh: 是冬，封泰山，命綸同計度發運事。

translations.literal: That winter, performing the Fengshan at Mount Tai, the Emperor ordered Lun jointly to plan transport and supply affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when the Emperor performed the Fengshan rite at Mount Tai, Lun was ordered to help plan transport and supply.

sentences.zh: 禮成，遷戶部郎中、直昭文館，待制如故。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed he was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Revenue with direct access to Zhaowen Hall; his status as academician remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: After the ceremony he was made Director of the Ministry of Revenue with access to the Zhaowen Hall, while retaining his academician title.

sentences.zh: 被詔，同編《東封祥瑞封禪記》。

translations.literal: He received an edict jointly to compile the Record of Eastern Fengshan Auspicious Responses and the Fengshan Rite.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to help compile the Record of Eastern Fengshan Auspicious Omens and the Fengshan Rite.

sentences.zh: 會峻待制之秩，又兼集賢殿修撰。

translations.literal: When the academician rank was elevated, he also concurrently served as Compiler of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: When the academician rank was raised in standing, he was also made compiler of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 建議修釋奠儀，頒於天下；

translations.literal: He proposed repairing the ceremony for the Confucian sacrifice and promulgating it throughout the realm;
translations.idiomatic: He proposed restoring the Confucian sacrifice rites and issuing them empire-wide;

sentences.zh: 立常平倉，隸司農寺，以平民糴，皆從之。

translations.literal: he established Ever-Normal Granaries subordinate to the Ministry of Agriculture to stabilize grain prices—all were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: and establishing Ever-Normal Granaries under the Ministry of Agriculture to stabilize grain prices—both measures were approved.

sentences.zh: 嘗宴餞种放於龍圖閣，詔近臣為序，上覽綸所作，稱其有史才。

translations.literal: Once, at a farewell banquet for Zhong Fang in the Dragon Diagram Hall, an edict ordered near ministers to write prefaces; the Emperor reading Lun's composition praised his talent for history.
translations.idiomatic: At a farewell feast for Zhong Fang in the Dragon Diagram Hall, senior officials were asked to write prefaces. The Emperor read Lun's piece and declared that he had a historian's gift.

sentences.zh: 三年，擢樞密直學士，上作詩寵之。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs; the Emperor composed a poem to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was elevated to Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and the Emperor wrote him a poem of favor.

sentences.zh: 祀汾陰，復領發運之職。

translations.literal: At the sacrifice at Fenyin he again headed transport and supply duties.
translations.idiomatic: During the Fenyin sacrifice he again oversaw transport and supply.

sentences.zh: 居無何，出知杭州，就加左司郎中。

translations.literal: Before long he was sent out as prefect of Hangzhou and concurrently promoted to Left Director in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was posted as prefect of Hangzhou and promoted to Left Director in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 屬江潮為患，乃立埽岸，以易柱石之製，雖免水患，而眾頗非其變法。

translations.literal: As river tides became a calamity, he built revetment embankments, replacing the pillar-and-stone method; though water disaster was avoided, many disapproved his changing the method.
translations.idiomatic: When tidal flooding threatened the city, he built brush-revetment dykes in place of the old pillar-and-stone works. The floods were checked, but many criticized the innovation.

sentences.zh: 胡則時領發運，嘗居杭州，肆縱不檢，厚結李溥，綸素惡之。

translations.literal: Hu Ze then headed transport, had once lived in Hangzhou, was unrestrained and undisciplined, and closely bonded with Li Pu—Lun had long detested him.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ze, then in charge of transport, had previously lived in Hangzhou, where he lived loosely and cultivated ties with Li Pu—men Lun had long despised.

sentences.zh: 通判吳耀卿，則之黨也，伺綸動靜，密以報則。

translations.literal: Vice-prefect Wu Yaoqing was Hu Ze's partisan; he watched Lun's movements and secretly reported to Ze.
translations.idiomatic: Vice-prefect Wu Yaoqing, a follower of Hu Ze, kept watch on Lun and secretly informed Ze of his actions.

sentences.zh: 則時為當塗者所昵，因共捃摭綸過，徙知揚州。

translations.literal: Ze was then favored by those in power; together they gathered Lun's faults, and he was moved to prefect of Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ze enjoyed favor with the powers at court; together they collected charges against Lun and had him transferred to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 惟揚亦溥、則巡內，持之益急，求改僻郡，徙徐州。

translations.literal: But Yang too lay within Pu and Ze's circuit—they pressed him all the more; he sought transfer to a remote prefecture and was moved to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yangzhou also fell within the orbit of Li Pu and Hu Ze, and their pressure only grew. Lun asked for a remote posting and was sent to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 八年，與劉綜並罷學士，授左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, together with Liu Zong, he was removed as academician and granted the post of Left Remonstrating Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he and Liu Zong were both stripped of their academician titles and appointed Left Remonstrating Grand Masters.

sentences.zh: 代還，復知青州。

translations.literal: When his term expired and he returned, he was again appointed prefect of Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After completing his tour of duty he returned to office and was again made prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，發公廩以救餓殍，全安甚眾。

translations.literal: In a year of famine he opened public granaries to save the starving dead; very many were wholly preserved in safety.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine he opened the public granaries to feed the starving, saving a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 徙鄆州，王遵誨為勸農副使，嘗佐西邊，寓家永興，閨門不肅，事將發，知府寇準為平之。

translations.literal: He was moved to Yan Prefecture; Wang Zunhui was Vice Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture, had once assisted on the western frontier, and kept his household at Yongxing—domestic discipline was lax; as the matter was about to break open, Prefect Kou Zhun settled it.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Yanzhou, he encountered Wang Zunhui, Vice Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture, a former western frontier officer whose family lived at Yongxing. Wang's household was disorderly; when scandal threatened to erupt, Prefect Kou Zhun intervened and smoothed the affair.

sentences.zh: 綸因戲謔語及準，遵誨恚怒，以為汙己，遂奏綸謗訕，坐左遷岳州團練副使，易和州。

translations.literal: Lun, in jesting banter, mentioned Zhun; Zunhui flew into rage, taking it as having stained himself, and memorialized that Lun had slandered and mocked him. For this Lun was demoted to Vice Commissioner of the Yuezhou Militia, then transferred to He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In playful talk Lun mentioned Kou Zhun; Wang Zunhui, furious at what he took as a slur on his honor, memorialized that Lun had slandered him. Lun was demoted to vice commissioner of the Yuezhou militia and later transferred to Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 天禧四年，改保靜軍副使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianxi, he was changed to Vice Commissioner of the Baojing Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxi 4 he was reassigned as vice commissioner of the Baojing Army.

sentences.zh: 是冬，以疾求歸故里，改太常少卿，分司南京。

translations.literal: That winter, because of illness he sought return to his native place; he was changed to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and assigned as nominal commissioner at the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, ill and longing for home, he was made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices with a nominal posting at the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died, age sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he died at sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 綸篤於古學，善談名理，喜言民政，頗近迂闊。

translations.literal: Lun was devoted to ancient learning, skilled at discussing principles of names, fond of speaking on civil administration, and rather inclined toward pedantic broadness.
translations.idiomatic: Lun was steeped in classical learning, fluent in philosophical principle, and eager to discuss public welfare—though his views could run toward the lofty and impractical.

sentences.zh: 事兄維友愛甚厚，維卒，訃聞，哀慟不食者數日。

translations.literal: In serving his elder brother Wei he was very warmly affectionate; when Wei died, upon news of death he grieved and did not eat for several days.
translations.idiomatic: He loved his elder brother Wei deeply; when Wei died and word reached him, he mourned so bitterly that he refused food for days.

sentences.zh: 與交遊故舊，以信義著稱。

translations.literal: Among friends and old acquaintances he was renowned for trustworthiness and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Among friends and old associates he was known above all for integrity and good faith.

sentences.zh: 士子謁見者，必詢其所業，訪其志尚，隨才誘誨之。

translations.literal: When scholar-gentlemen came to call on him, he would always inquire into their studies and investigate their aspirations, guiding and instructing each according to talent.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever young scholars came to see him, he asked what they were studying, what they hoped to become, and guided each according to his gifts.

sentences.zh: 嘗云：「歸老後，得十年在鄉閭講習，亦可以恢道濟世。」

translations.literal: He once said: "After retiring in old age, if I could have ten years teaching in the village community, that too could expand the Way and benefit the world."
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "If in retirement I could spend ten years teaching in my home district, that alone might widen the Way and serve the age."

sentences.zh: 大中祥符中，繼修禮文之事，綸悉參其議，與陳彭年並職，屢召對，多建條式，恩寵甚盛。

translations.literal: In Dazhong Xiangfu, when continuing work on ritual texts, Lun fully participated in the deliberations, shared duties with Chen Pengnian, was repeatedly summoned for audience, proposed many regulations, and enjoyed abundant imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: During Dazhong Xiangfu, when court ritual was being revised, Lun took part in every debate, served alongside Chen Pengnian, was often called to audience, drafted many rules, and enjoyed extraordinary favor.

sentences.zh: 樂於薦士，每一奏十數人，皆當時知名士。

translations.literal: He delighted in recommending scholars; each memorial listed more than ten men, all notable gentlemen of the day.
translations.idiomatic: He loved recommending talent and would often submit more than ten names at once—every one a distinguished man of the time.

sentences.zh: 晚節為權幸所排，遂不復振。

translations.literal: In his later years he was ousted by the powerful and favored, and never recovered his standing.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years the court favorites pushed him aside, and he never regained his former influence.

sentences.zh: 善訓子弟，雖至清顯，不改其純儉。

translations.literal: He was skilled at instructing sons and younger kin; though he rose to pure and eminent rank, he did not alter his simple frugality.
translations.idiomatic: He trained his sons and nephews well; even after reaching high and honored office he kept the same plain, frugal ways.

sentences.zh: 既沒，家無餘貲。

translations.literal: After his death the family had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his household had nothing left over.

sentences.zh: 張知白時知府事，輟奉以助其喪。

translations.literal: When Zhang Zhibai was handling prefectural affairs, he contributed from his salary to help with the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhibai, then administering the prefecture, gave part of his own salary to help pay for the burial.

sentences.zh: 家人於几閣間，得《遺戒》一篇，大率皆誘勸為學。

translations.literal: The family found among his desk and shelves a piece titled Testamentary Admonitions, which for the most part urged and encouraged pursuit of learning.
translations.idiomatic: Among his desk and shelves the family found a Testamentary Admonition, mostly exhorting his descendants to devote themselves to study.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected writings in twenty fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works in twenty fascicles.

sentences.zh: 又前後奏議，有機務利害、備邊均田之策，別為《論思集》十卷，分上下篇。

translations.literal: Also memorials submitted before and after, containing policies on state affairs' benefits and harms and on border defense and equal-field measures, were separately titled Collected Deliberations in ten fascicles, divided into upper and lower parts.
translations.idiomatic: His earlier and later policy memorials—on statecraft, frontier defense, and equal-field policy—were gathered separately as Collected Deliberations in ten fascicles, in two parts.

sentences.zh: 天聖中，其子舜賓獻之，詔贈左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In Tiansheng his son Shunbin presented them; an edict posthumously granted him Left Remonstrating Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiansheng era his son Shunbin presented the collection, and the throne posthumously honored Lun as Left Remonstrating Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 舜賓，官太子中舍。

translations.literal: Shunbin served as Palace Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Shunbin held the post of palace attendant to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 張去華

translations.literal: Zhang Quhua
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Quhua

sentences.zh: 張去華，字信臣，開封襄邑人。

translations.literal: Zhang Quhua, courtesy name Xinchen, was a native of Xiangyi in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Quhua, styled Xinchen, came from Xiangyi in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 父誼，字希賈。

translations.literal: His father Yi, courtesy name Xijia.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhang Yi, styled Xijia.

sentences.zh: 好學，不事產業。

translations.literal: Fond of learning, he did not attend to property and estates.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books and cared nothing for managing the family holdings.

sentences.zh: 既孤，諸父使督耕隴上，他日往視之，見閱書於樹下，怒其不親穡事，詬辱之。

translations.literal: After being orphaned, his uncles had him supervise farming in the fields; one day when they went to inspect him, they found him reading books under a tree, and angered that he did not personally attend to the harvest, they reviled and insulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned early, he was put by his uncles to oversee work in the fields. When they came to check on him one day and found him reading under a tree instead of tending the crop, they cursed and humiliated him.

sentences.zh: 誼謂其兄曰：「若不就學於外，素志無成矣。」

translations.literal: Yi said to his elder brother: "If I do not go to study outside, my lifelong aspiration will never be fulfilled."
translations.idiomatic: Yi told his elder brother, "Unless I go away to study, the ambition I have nursed all my life will come to nothing."

sentences.zh: 遂潛詣洛陽龍門書院，與宗人沆、鸞、湜結友，故名聞都下。

translations.literal: He then secretly went to Longmen Academy in Luoyang, befriended clansmen Hang, Luan, and Shi, and thus his name became known in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: So he stole away to Longmen Academy in Luoyang, befriended his kinsmen Hang, Luan, and Shi, and soon his name was known throughout the capital.

sentences.zh: 長興中，和凝掌貢舉，誼舉進士，調補耀州團練推官。

translations.literal: In the Changxing era He Ning presided over the examinations; Yi passed the jinshi and was assigned as push officer of the militia commission at Yao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During Changxing, when He Ning ran the examinations, Yi passed the jinshi and was appointed push officer on the Yao Prefecture militia staff.

sentences.zh: 晉天福初，代還。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Later Jin Tianfu his term expired and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Later Jin Tianfu era he finished his tour and returned.

sentences.zh: 會凝由內署拜端明殿學士，署門不接賓客，誼聞之，即日致書於凝，以為「切近之職，實當顧問，四方利害，所宜詢訪，若不接賓客，聾瞽耳目，坐虧職業，雖為自安計，其可得乎？」

translations.literal: When Ning was appointed from the inner secretariat as Academician of the Hall of Clear Brilliance, his office gate did not receive guests. Yi, hearing this, that same day sent a letter to Ning, stating: "A post close at hand truly should be consulted; the benefits and harms of the four directions ought to be inquired into. If you do not receive guests, you deafen and blind your ears and eyes, thereby falling short in your duty — even as a plan for your own ease, how can that succeed?"
translations.idiomatic: When Ning left the inner secretariat to become an academician of the Hall of Clear Brilliance, he closed his gate to visitors. Yi heard of it and wrote to him the same day: "In a post so close to power you are meant to advise the throne and hear what matters in every quarter. Shut your door to guests and you deafen yourself to the realm—and fail in your office. Even as a way to keep your peace, how can that work?"

sentences.zh: 凝大奇之，他日，薦於宰相桑維翰曰：「凝門生中有張誼者，性介直，頗涉辭藝，可備諫職。」

translations.literal: Ning was greatly astonished by this; another day he recommended him to Chancellor Sang Weihan, saying: "Among Ning's disciples is one Zhang Yi — upright by nature, fairly versed in rhetoric and the arts; he can fill a remonstrance post."
translations.idiomatic: Ning was astonished. Later he recommended Yi to Chancellor Sang Weihan: "Among my students is Zhang Yi—frank by nature and well read in letters. He is fit for remonstrance office."

sentences.zh: 未幾，超拜左拾遺。

translations.literal: Before long he was suddenly promoted to Left Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yi was abruptly promoted to Left Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 誼以晉室新造，典禮未完，數上章請復有唐故事。

translations.literal: Yi, because the Jin house was newly established and its ritual codes incomplete, repeatedly submitted memorials requesting restoration of Tang precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Jin dynasty was new and its rites still incomplete, Yi repeatedly memorialized to restore Tang practice.

sentences.zh: 又言契丹有援立之助，所宜敦信謹備，不可自逸，以啟釁端。

translations.literal: He also said that the Khitans had assisted in enthronement and ought to be treated with earnest trust and careful guard; one must not relax oneself and thereby open the way to provocation.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that the Khitans had helped put the dynasty on the throne and deserved steadfast trust and vigilance—that slackness on China's part would only invite trouble.

sentences.zh: 改右補闕，充集賢殿修撰，歷禮部員外郎、侍御史。

translations.literal: He was changed to Right Supplementation Censor, served as Compiler of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and passed through Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Right Supplementation Censor and compiler of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and later served as vice director of the Ministry of Rites and censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 改倉部、知制誥，加禮部郎中。

translations.literal: He was changed to the Warehouse Department, served as drafter of edicts, and was given the added title of Ministry of Rites Director.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to the Warehouse Department, became a drafter of edicts, and was also named director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 乾祐初，真拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyou he was truly appointed Central Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Qianyou he received formal appointment as a drafter of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時蘇逢吉、楊邠、王章輩攀附漢祖，驟得大用，搢紳多附之，誼不為屈，故共嫉之。

translations.literal: At the time Su Fengji, Yang Bin, Wang Zhang, and the like clung to the Han founder and suddenly gained great employment; gentry largely attached to them, but Yi would not yield, so together they envied him.
translations.idiomatic: Su Fengji, Yang Bin, Wang Zhang, and their circle had risen fast by clinging to the Han founder, and most officials courted them. Yi would not bend, and they came to hate him for it.

sentences.zh: 遣誼為吳越宣諭使，與兵部郎中馬承翰同往賜官告。

translations.literal: They dispatched Yi as Exhortation Commissioner to Wu-Yue, together with Ministry of War Director Ma Chenghan to go and bestow patent of office.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Yi as imperial envoy to Wu and Yue, with Ma Chenghan of the Ministry of War, to deliver patents of appointment.

sentences.zh: 浙人每迓朝使，必列步騎以自誇詫，誼與承翰竊笑之。

translations.literal: People of Zhe, whenever they received imperial envoys, would array infantry and cavalry to boast; Yi and Chenghan secretly laughed at this.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Zhe received a court envoy, the locals would parade foot and horse to show off; Yi and Chenghan laughed quietly among themselves.

sentences.zh: 又乘酒，言詞有輕發者，錢俶甚恥之，乃奏誼擅箠防援官。

translations.literal: Again, under the influence of wine his words had some lightly spoken remarks; Qian Chu was deeply shamed by this and memorialized that Yi had arbitrarily beaten the escort officer.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, he let slip words that cut too lightly; Qian Chu, deeply embarrassed, memorialized that Yi had beaten an escort officer without cause.

sentences.zh: 又夜集，與承翰使酒，語相侵，坐貶均州司戶，改房州司馬，歲餘卒。

translations.literal: Again one night at a gathering he made wine with Chenghan and their words mutually attacked each other; for this he was demoted to Registrar of Jun Prefecture, changed to Vice Magistrate of Fang Prefecture, and after a year plus died.
translations.idiomatic: Another night he and Chenghan drank together until their talk turned vicious; Yi was demoted to registrar of Junzhou, then vice magistrate of Fangzhou, and died a little over a year later.

sentences.zh: 去華幼勵學，敏於屬辭，以蔭補太廟齋郎。

translations.literal: Quhua from youth urged himself in study, was quick at composing text, and by hereditary privilege was appointed Fast-officer of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Quhua drove himself to study from boyhood, wrote with ease, and entered office by privilege as a fast-officer of the imperial ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 周世宗平淮南，去華時年十八，慨然歎曰：「兵戰未息，民事不修，非馭國持久之術。」

translations.literal: When Later Zhou Shizong pacified Huainan, Quhua was then eighteen; he sighed with emotion and said: "Warfare has not ceased, and civil affairs are not repaired — this is not a lasting method of governing a state."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong of Later Zhou pacified Huainan, Quhua was eighteen. He sighed and said, "While war never ends and the people's affairs lie neglected, no state can endure."

sentences.zh: 因著《南征賦》、《治民論》，獻於行在。

translations.literal: Thereupon he composed Rhapsody on the Southern Expedition and Discourse on Governing the People and presented them at the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote the Rhapsody on the Southern Expedition and Discourse on Governing the People and submitted them to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 召試，授御史臺主簿。

translations.literal: He was summoned for examination and granted Chief Clerk of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned for an examination, he was made chief clerk of the censorate.

sentences.zh: 屬三院議事，不得預坐，謂所親曰：「簿領之職，非壯夫所為。」

translations.literal: When the three bureaus deliberated affairs he could not take a seat in the meeting; he said to those close to him: "The work of ledgers and documents is not what a robust man should do."
translations.idiomatic: When the three censorial bureaus met to decide cases he was not allowed a seat. He told those close to him, "Paperwork is no work for a man in his prime."

sentences.zh: 即棄官歸鄭州，杜門不出者三載。

translations.literal: He immediately resigned office and returned to Zheng Prefecture, shutting his door and not going out for three years.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned at once, went home to Zhengzhou, and kept his doors closed for three years.

sentences.zh: 建隆初，始攜文遊京師，大為李昉所稱。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianlong he first carried his writings to the capital, where he was greatly praised by Li Fang.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jianlong he took his writings to the capital and won high praise from Li Fang.

sentences.zh: 明年，舉進士甲科，即拜秘書郎、直史館。

translations.literal: The next year he passed the jinshi in the top grade and was immediately appointed Secretariat Officer and Associate at the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he took jinshi honors in the top grade and was at once made a secretariat officer and historiography associate.

sentences.zh: 以歲滿不遷，上章自訴，因言制誥張澹、盧多遜、殿中侍御史蘇頌文學膚淺，願得校其優劣。

translations.literal: Because his term was full yet he was not promoted, he submitted a memorial complaining on his own behalf, and also said that edict drafters Zhang Tan and Lu Duoxun and Palace Censor Su Song had shallow literary learning, and he wished to compare their relative merit.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended without promotion he memorialized in his own defense, declaring that the drafters Zhang Tan and Lu Duoxun and palace censor Su Song were shallow scholars—and asking for a test to settle who was better.

sentences.zh: 太祖立召澹輩與去華臨軒策試，命陶穀等考之。

translations.literal: Taizu immediately summoned Tan and the others with Quhua for a policy examination before the throne and ordered Tao Gu and others to grade them.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu at once summoned Tan and the rest with Quhua to an examination before the throne and put Tao Gu and others in charge of judging the results.

sentences.zh: 澹以所對不應問，降秩，即擢去華為右補闕，賜襲衣、銀帶、鞍勒馬。

translations.literal: Tan, because his answers did not fit the questions, was reduced in rank; Quhua was immediately elevated to Right Supplementation Censor and granted formal court robes, a silver belt, and a saddled horse.
translations.idiomatic: Tan, whose answers missed the questions, was demoted; Quhua was promptly raised to Right Supplementation Censor and given court dress, a silver belt, and a saddled horse.

sentences.zh: 朝議薄其躁進，以是不遷秩者十六年。

translations.literal: Court opinion looked down on his hasty advancement, and for this reason he received no promotion in rank for sixteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Official opinion scorned his pushiness, and for sixteen years he received no further promotion.

sentences.zh: 嘗得對便殿，詢及家世，遂訴父始忤權貴，因罹重貶。

translations.literal: Once he was granted audience in the Convenient Hall; the Emperor inquired into his family background, and he thereupon complained that his father at first had offended the powerful and consequently suffered severe demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Once, received in the Convenient Hall, he was asked about his family and told how his father had first offended the mighty and been harshly banished.

sentences.zh: 宰相薛居正亦為言之，太祖為之動容，且曰：「漢室不道，奸臣擅權，此朕所親見也。」

translations.literal: Chancellor Xue Juzheng also spoke on his behalf; Taizu was moved and said: "The Han house was without the Way; wicked ministers monopolized power — this I personally witnessed."
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Xue Juzheng added his voice, and Taizu was moved. "The Han court lost the Way," he said, "and wicked ministers seized power—I saw it with my own eyes."

sentences.zh: 荊湖平，命通判道州。

translations.literal: When Jinghu was pacified, he was ordered to serve as Vice-prefect of Dao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Jinghu was pacified he was appointed vice-prefect of Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 去華上言：「桂管為五嶺衝要，令劉鋹保境固守，賴之為捍蔽，若大軍先克其城，以趣番禺，如踐無人之境。」

translations.literal: Quhua submitted a memorial saying: "The Guiguan circuit is the vital passage of the Five Ridges; now Liu Chang holds his territory and firmly defends it — relying on this as a shield and barrier; if the great army first takes his city and then presses on toward Panyu, it will be like treading a land without men."
translations.idiomatic: Quhua memorialized: "Guiguan is the key to the Five Ridges. Liu Chang now holds his domain and stands firm, and that very barrier shields us. If the main army first takes his city and then marches on Panyu, the advance will be like walking through empty country."

sentences.zh: 且言桂州可取之狀，有詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: He also set forth the circumstances in which Gui Prefecture could be taken; an edict praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: He also explained how Guizhou could be seized, and the throne answered with praise and reward.

sentences.zh: 代還，知磁、乾二州，選為益州通判，遷起居舍人、知鳳翔府。

translations.literal: When his term expired and he returned, he governed Ci and Qian Prefectures, was selected as Vice-prefect of Yi Prefecture, and was promoted to Diarist and Prefect of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: After his tour he served as prefect of Ci and Qian, was chosen vice-prefect of Yizhou, and rose to diarist and prefect of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 從太宗征太原，監隨駕左藏庫，就命為京東轉運使。

translations.literal: Following Taizong's expedition against Taiyuan, he supervised the Left Treasury accompanying the imperial train, and was thereupon appointed Transport Commissioner of the Eastern Capital Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On Taizong's campaign against Taiyuan he oversaw the left treasury in the imperial train and was then made transport commissioner for the Eastern Capital circuit.

sentences.zh: 歷左司員外郎、禮部郎中。

translations.literal: He passed through Left Secretariat Vice Director and Ministry of Rites Director.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as left secretariat vice director and director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 太平興國七年，為江南轉運使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taiping Xingguo he was Transport Commissioner of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 7 he became Jiangnan transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，王師討幽州，去華督宋州饋運至拒馬河，就命掌河北轉運事。

translations.literal: In Yongxi, when imperial forces attacked Youzhou, Quhua supervised supply transport from Song Prefecture to the Juma River, and was thereupon appointed to manage Hebei transport affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongxi, when the court marched on Youzhou, Quhua drove supplies from Songzhou to the Juma River and was then put in charge of Hebei transport.

sentences.zh: 三年，知陝州，未行，著《大政要錄》三十篇以獻，上覽而嘉之，詔書褒美，賜采五十匹，因留不遣。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed prefect of Shan Prefecture; before departing he composed Essential Records of Great Governance in thirty chapters and presented them; the Emperor read and praised them, an edict praised him, and granted fifty bolts of colored silk — and kept him without sending him away.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was named prefect of Shanzhou. Before leaving he submitted Essential Records of Great Governance in thirty chapters. The emperor read them with approval, issued a commendation, gave him fifty bolts of colored silk—and kept him at court.

sentences.zh: 會許王尹京，命為開封府判官，殿中侍御史陳載為推官，並賜金紫。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Xu was governing the capital, he was appointed Judge of Kaifeng Prefecture, with Palace Censor Chen Zai as investigating officer; both were granted gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Xu governed the capital, Quhua was made judge of Kaifeng Prefecture with palace censor Chen Zai as investigating officer; both received gold-and-purple insignia.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「卿等皆朝之端士，特加選用，其善佐吾子。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said to them: "You are all outstanding gentlemen of the court, specially chosen; do well in assisting my son."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told them, "You are men of the first rank at court, chosen on purpose—serve my son well."

sentences.zh: 各賜錢百萬。

translations.literal: Each was granted a million in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Each was also given a million cash.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，就拜左諫議大夫，又令樞密使王顯傳旨，諭以輔成之意。

translations.literal: After a year he was directly appointed Left Remonstrating Grand Master, and again the Bureau of Military Affairs Commissioner Wang Xian transmitted an imperial message instructing him in the intent to assist in his completion.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made Left Remonstrating Grand Master outright, and Military Affairs Commissioner Wang Xian brought a further message urging him to help the prince mature.

sentences.zh: 未幾，有廬州尼道安訟弟婦不實，府不為治，械繫送本州。

translations.literal: Before long, a nun Da'an of Luzhou sued her sister-in-law on false grounds; the prefecture would not handle it and had her shackled and sent to the home prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Luzhou nun Da'an brought a false suit against her sister-in-law. The prefecture refused to act and had Da'an bound and sent back to her home district.

sentences.zh: 弟婦即徐鉉妻之甥。

translations.literal: The sister-in-law was the niece of Xu Xuan's wife.
translations.idiomatic: The sister-in-law was a niece of Xu Xuan's wife.

sentences.zh: 道安伐登聞鼓，言鉉以尺牘求請，去華故不為治。

translations.literal: Da'an struck the Petition Drum at the Gate of Exalted Renown, saying Xuan had sought favors by letter and Quhua therefore would not try the case.
translations.idiomatic: Da'an beat the Petition Drum at the Gate of Exalted Renown, claiming Xu Xuan had written asking favor and that Quhua had refused the case for that reason.

sentences.zh: 上怒，去華坐削一任，貶安州司馬。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry; Quhua was punished by having one appointment stricken and was demoted to Vice Magistrate of An Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious. Quhua lost one rank and was demoted to vice magistrate of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，召授將作少監、知興元府，未行，改晉州。

translations.literal: After a year plus he was summoned and granted Vice Director of Imperial Construction and Prefect of Xingyuan; before departing he was changed to Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After a little more than a year he was recalled, made vice director of imperial construction and prefect of Xingyuan, then reassigned to Jinzhou before he could leave.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書少監、知許州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Prefect of Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the secretariat and prefect of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 真宗嗣位，復拜左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong succeeded to the throne, he was again appointed Left Remonstrating Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong came to the throne Quhua was again made Left Remonstrating Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷給事中、知杭州。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Supervising Secretary and Prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he rose to supervising secretary and prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 兩浙自錢氏賦民丁錢，有死而不免者，去華建議請除之，有司以經費所仰，固執不許。

translations.literal: In the two Zhes since the Qian clan levied a per-capita tax on registered males, there were cases where the dead were not exempted; Quhua proposed requesting its abolition, but the relevant offices, because finances depended on it, stubbornly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Qian regime the Two Zhes had levied a head tax on every registered male, even after death. Quhua asked that it be abolished, but the agencies, clinging to the revenue, would not agree.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，徙蘇州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping he was transferred to Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 2 he was moved to Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 頃之，以疾求分司西京。

translations.literal: Before long, due to illness he requested assignment as nominal commissioner at the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, ill, he asked for a nominal post at the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 在洛葺園廬，作中隱亭以見志。

translations.literal: While in Luoyang he repaired garden lodges and built the Central Reclusion Pavilion to express his intent.
translations.idiomatic: In Luoyang he restored a garden house and built the Central Reclusion Pavilion to show where his heart lay.

sentences.zh: 景德元年，改工部侍郎致仕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingde he was changed to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and retired.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde 1 he was made vice director of the Ministry of Works and retired.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: In the third year he died, age sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he died at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 去華美姿貌，善談論，有蘊藉，頗尚氣節。

translations.literal: Quhua had handsome looks, was skilled at discourse, possessed restrained elegance, and rather cherished integrity and principle.
translations.idiomatic: Quhua was handsome, eloquent, and quietly polished, with a strong sense of honor.

sentences.zh: 在營道得父同門生何氏二子，教其學問。

translations.literal: While at Yingdao he obtained two sons of the He family, fellow students of his father, and taught them learning.
translations.idiomatic: At Yingdao he took in two sons of the He family, his father's old schoolmates, and taught them himself.

sentences.zh: 受代，攜之京師，慰薦館穀，並登仕籍。

translations.literal: When his term ended he brought them to the capital, comforted them, recommended them, provided lodging and grain, and both entered the rolls of office.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he brought them to the capital, saw to their lodging and keep, recommended them, and both won places in office.

sentences.zh: 嘗獻《元元論》，大旨以養民務穡為急，真宗深所嘉賞，命以縑素寫其論為十八軸，列置龍圖閣之四壁。

translations.literal: He once presented Discourse on the Primordial People; its main point was that nourishing the people and urgent attention to agriculture were paramount. Zhenzong deeply praised it and ordered the discourse copied on silk in eighteen scrolls and arrayed on the four walls of the Dragon Diagram Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He once submitted the Discourse on the Primordial People, arguing that feeding the people and putting agriculture first were the urgent tasks of rule. Zhenzong admired it deeply and had the text copied in eighteen silk scrolls and hung on the four walls of the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 然不飾邊幅，頗為清議所貶，以是不登顯用。

translations.literal: Yet he did not trim his appearance; pure opinion rather belittled him, and for this he did not rise to eminent employment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he cared little for dress or decorum, and respectable opinion looked down on him—so he never reached the highest posts.

sentences.zh: 有集十五卷。

translations.literal: He had collected writings in fifteen fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in fifteen fascicles.

sentences.zh: 子：師古至國子博士、師錫殿中丞、師顏國子博士。

translations.literal: Sons: Shigu reached Erudite of the Imperial Academy; Shixi, Palace Aide; Shiyan, Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Shigu, who rose to erudite of the imperial academy; Shixi, palace aide; and Shiyan, also an imperial academy erudite.

sentences.zh: 子 師德

translations.literal: Son: Shide
translations.idiomatic: Son: Shide

sentences.zh: 師德，字尚賢。

translations.literal: Shide, courtesy name Shangxian.
translations.idiomatic: Shide, styled Shangxian.

sentences.zh: 去華十子，最器師德。

translations.literal: Of Quhua's ten sons, he most prized Shide.
translations.idiomatic: Of Quhua's ten sons he valued Shide most.

sentences.zh: 嘗欲任以官，辭不就。

translations.literal: He once wished to appoint him to office, but Shide declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Quhua once tried to give him office, but Shide refused.

sentences.zh: 去華曰：「此兒必繼吾志。」

translations.literal: Quhua said: "This boy will surely carry on my aspirations."
translations.idiomatic: Quhua said, "This boy will surely carry on what I live for."

sentences.zh: 真宗祀汾陰，知河南府薛映薦其學行，又獻《汾陰大禮頌》於行在。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong performed the sacrifice at Fenyin, Prefect of Henan Fu Xue Ying recommended his scholarship and conduct, and he also presented Eulogy of the Great Rite at Fenyin at the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong sacrificed at Fenyin, Xue Ying, prefect of Henan, praised his learning and character, and Shide also presented his Eulogy of the Great Rite at Fenyin to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 是歲，舉進士亦為第一，時人榮之。

translations.literal: That year he also passed the jinshi as first place, and men of the time counted it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he took first place on the jinshi examination, to the envy of his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 除將作監丞、通判耀州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of Imperial Construction and Vice-prefect of Yao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice director of imperial construction and vice-prefect of Yaozhou.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書省著作郎、集賢校理、判三司都理欠憑由司。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Compiler in the Secretariat, Collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and Judge of the Three Offices General Office for Overdue Vouchers.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to secretariat compiler, collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and judge of the Three Offices office for overdue vouchers.

sentences.zh: 建言：「有逋負官物而被繫，本非侵盜，若煢獨貧病無以自償，願特蠲之。」

translations.literal: He offered a proposal: "Those who owe state goods and are imprisoned — the debt itself is not invasion or theft; if they are solitary, poor, and ill and cannot repay on their own, I wish they may be specially remitted.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed: "When men are jailed for debts to the state though they never stole the goods, and when the poor, sick, and alone cannot pay, I ask that such debts be forgiven outright.

sentences.zh: 帝用其言。

translations.literal: The emperor adopted his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 嘗奏事殿中，帝訪以時事，而條對甚備。

translations.literal: Once when memorializing in the hall, the emperor questioned him on current affairs, and he answered in detailed items very completely.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion he presented business in the hall; the emperor asked his views on current affairs, and he replied point by point with thorough completeness.

sentences.zh: 帝喜曰：「朕藩邸知卿父名，今又知卿才。」

translations.literal: The emperor said with pleasure: "At my princely residence I knew your father's name; now I also know your talent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said delightedly, "When I was in my princely residence I knew your father's name; now I know your gifts as well."

sentences.zh: 其後每遣使，帝輒曰：「張師德可用。」

translations.literal: Thereafter, whenever envoys were dispatched, the emperor would always say: "Zhang Shide is fit for use."
translations.idiomatic: From then on, whenever the court sent out envoys, the emperor would say, "Zhang Shide will do."

sentences.zh: 契丹、高麗使來，多以師德主之。

translations.literal: When Khitan and Goryeo envoys came, Shide was mostly put in charge of receiving them.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan and Goryeo missions were mostly entrusted to Shide.

sentences.zh: 天禧初，安撫淮南，苦風眩，改判司農寺。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxi, he pacified Huainan, suffered from dizziness and vertigo, and was transferred to serve as judge of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianxi era he was sent to pacify Huainan; afflicted by dizziness, he was reassigned to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 擢右正言、知制誥，判尚書刑部。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Rectifier and Drafting Edict, and judge of the Ministry of Justice in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to right rectifier and drafter of edicts, with concurrent duty as judge of the secretariat ministry of justice.

sentences.zh: 頃之，出知潁州，遷刑部員外郎、判大理寺，為群牧使、景靈宮判官，再遷吏部郎中。

translations.literal: Before long, he went out as prefect of Ying Prefecture, was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice and judge of the Court of Judicial Review, served as Commissioner of Pasture Administration and judge of Jingling Palace, and was promoted again to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made prefect of Yingzhou, then vice director of justice and judge of the Court of Judicial Review, commissioner of pasture administration and judge of Jingling Palace, and finally director in the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 以疾，知鄧州，徙汝州，拜左諫議大夫，罷知制誥。

translations.literal: Because of illness, he was assigned as prefect of Deng Prefecture, transferred to Ru Prefecture, appointed Left Remonstrance Censor, and removed from Drafting Edict.
translations.idiomatic: Illness led to appointments as prefect of Dengzhou and then Ruzhou; he was made left remonstrance censor and relieved of his duties drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 師德孝謹有家法，不交權貴，時相頗不悅之。

translations.literal: Shide was filial and scrupulous and observed family discipline; he did not associate with powerful persons, and the chief minister of the time was quite displeased with him.
translations.idiomatic: Shide was filial, cautious, and governed by strict family rules; he kept his distance from the powerful, which the reigning chief minister resented.

sentences.zh: 然亦多病，在西掖九年不遷，卒於官。

translations.literal: Yet he was also often ill; for nine years in the western secretariat he received no promotion, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was often ill as well; he spent nine years in the western secretariat without advancement and died in office.

sentences.zh: 有文集十卷。

translations.literal: He had collected writings in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings ran to ten juan.

sentences.zh: 子景憲，為太中大夫。

translations.literal: His son Jingxian served as Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingxian rose to grand master of the palace.

sentences.zh: 樂黃目

translations.literal: Le Huangmu
translations.idiomatic: Le Huangmu

sentences.zh: 樂黃目，字公禮，撫州宜黃人。

translations.literal: Le Huangmu, courtesy name Gongli, was a native of Yihuang in Fuz Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Le Huangmu, styled Gongli, came from Yihuang in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 世仕江左李氏。

translations.literal: For generations his family served the Li of Jiangzuo.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had served the Li of Jiangzuo for generations.

sentences.zh: 父史，字子正。

translations.literal: His father Shi, courtesy name Zizheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shi, styled Zizheng,

sentences.zh: 齊王景達鎮臨川，召掌奏箋，授秘書郎。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qi Jingda governed Linchuan, Shi was summoned to manage memorials and letters and was appointed Secretary Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qi, Jingda, held Linchuan, Shi was called to draft memorials and was made a secretary gentleman.

sentences.zh: 入朝，為平原主簿。

translations.literal: He entered court and served as registrar of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After entering court service he became registrar of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 太平興國五年，與顏明遠、劉昌言、張觀並以見任官舉進士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo, together with Yan Mingyuan, Liu Changyan, and Zhang Guan, all were nominated for the jinshi as incumbents in office.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 5 he was nominated for the jinshi together with Yan Mingyuan, Liu Changyan, and Zhang Guan, all as serving officials.

sentences.zh: 太宗惜科第不與，但授諸道掌書記。

translations.literal: Taizong regretted not granting examination rank, but only appointed them as secretaries for the various circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong withheld examination honors but appointed them secretaries on the various circuits.

sentences.zh: 史得佐武成軍，既而復賜及第。

translations.literal: Shi was assigned to assist the Wucheng Army; afterward he was again granted pass of the degree.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was posted to the Wucheng Army staff and later was granted examination standing after all.

sentences.zh: 上書言事，擢為著作佐郎、知陵州，獻《金明池賦》，召為三館編修。

translations.literal: He memorialized on affairs of state, was promoted to Assistant Compiler and prefect of Ling Prefecture, presented Fu of Jinming Pool, and was summoned as compiler of the Three Institutes.
translations.idiomatic: After memorializing on state affairs he was made assistant compiler and prefect of Lingzhou; his Fu of Jinming Pool won him appointment as a compiler in the Three Institutes.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，獻所著《貢舉事》二十卷，《登科記》三十卷，《題解》二十卷，《唐登科文選》五十卷，《孝弟錄》二十卷，《續卓異記》三卷。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi, he presented his Examination Affairs in twenty juan, Record of Successful Candidates in thirty juan, Explications in twenty juan, Anthology of Tang Examination Literature in fifty juan, Record of Filial Piety and Brotherly Duty in twenty juan, and Continuation of Record of Outstanding Worthies in three juan.
