translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 3 he submitted his own Examination Affairs (20 juan), Record of Successful Candidates (30 juan), Explications (20 juan), Anthology of Tang Examination Literature (50 juan), Record of Filial Piety and Brotherly Duty (20 juan), and Continuation of Record of Outstanding Worthies (3 juan).

sentences.zh: 太宗嘉其勤，遷著作郎、直史館。

translations.literal: Taizong praised his diligence and promoted him to Compiler and straight officer of the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong commended his industry and made him compiler and a straight officer of the historiography institute.

sentences.zh: 轉太常博士、知舒州，遷水部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and prefect of Shu Prefecture, and promoted to Vice Director of the Water Works.
translations.idiomatic: He became an erudite of the court of imperial sacrifices and prefect of Shuzhou, then vice director in the waterworks bureau.

sentences.zh: 淳化四年春，與司封員外郎、直昭文館李蕤同使兩浙巡撫，加都官、知黃州。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year of Chunhua, together with Vice Director of the Bureau of Awards and straight officer of the Zhaowen Institute Li Rui he was dispatched as envoy to tour and pacify Liangzhe, and was given added rank as director of the Bureau of Capital Affairs and prefect of Huang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Chunhua 4 he and Li Rui, vice director of the bureau of awards and straight officer of the Zhaowen Institute, toured and pacified the Liangzhe region; he was given added rank as capital-affairs director and prefect of Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 又獻《廣孝傳》五十卷，《總仙記》一百四十一卷。

translations.literal: He also presented Expanded Biographies of Filial Piety in fifty juan and Comprehensive Record of Immortals in one hundred forty-one juan.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted Expanded Biographies of Filial Piety (50 juan) and Comprehensive Record of Immortals (141 juan).

sentences.zh: 詔秘閣寫本進內。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Secret Repository to copy the manuscripts and present them within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the secret repository to transcribe the works and send them into the palace.

sentences.zh: 史好著述，然博而寡要，以五帝、三王，皆云仙去，論者嗤其詭誕。

translations.literal: Shi loved composing texts, yet his work was broad but lacked essentials; he held that the Five Emperors and Three Kings all departed as immortals, and commentators ridiculed this as bizarre and absurd.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was devoted to writing, but his works sprawled without focus; his claim that the Five Emperors and Three Kings all ascended as immortals made critics laugh at him as a fabulist.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，遷職方，復獻《廣孝新書》五十卷，《上清文苑》四十卷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping, he was transferred to the Bureau of Appointments, and again presented Expanded Filial Piety New Book in fifty juan and Shangqing Literary Grove in forty juan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianping he moved to the bureau of appointments and submitted Expanded Filial Piety: New Book (50 juan) and Shangqing Literary Grove (40 juan).

sentences.zh: 出知商州。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Shang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Shangzhou.

sentences.zh: 史前後臨民，頗以賄聞。

translations.literal: When Shi governed the people on various assignments, he was rather known for taking bribes.
translations.idiomatic: In his successive provincial posts Shi gained a reputation for graft.

sentences.zh: 俄以老疾為言，聽解職，分司西京。

translations.literal: Soon, citing old age and illness, he was permitted to resign his post and was assigned to nominal duty in the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He soon pleaded age and illness, was allowed to leave office, and was given nominal posting in the western capital.

sentences.zh: 五年，郊祀畢，奉留守司表入賀，因得召對。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, after the suburban sacrifice was completed, he submitted a congratulatory memorial through the capital-resident office and thereby gained a summoned audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, after the suburban sacrifice, he entered a congratulatory memorial through the western-capital resident office and was summoned to audience.

sentences.zh: 上見其矍鑠不衰，又知篤學，盡取所著書藏秘府，復授舊職，與黃目同在文館，人以為榮。

translations.literal: The emperor saw that he was vigorous and undiminished, and knowing his earnest scholarship, took all his writings for the secret repository, restored his former post, and Huangmu was also in the literary institutes — men considered it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Finding him still vigorous and knowing his lifelong devotion to learning, the emperor placed all his books in the secret repository, restored his old post, and kept Huangmu in the literary institutes as well — an honor people envied.

sentences.zh: 出掌西京磨勘司，黃目為京西轉運。

translations.literal: He went out to head the Western Capital merit review office, and Huangmu served as transport commissioner for the Western Capital circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was put in charge of the western capital merit-review office while Huangmu served as transport commissioner for the western capital circuit.

sentences.zh: 改判留司御史臺。

translations.literal: He was transferred to judge the capital-resident Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to judge the capital-resident censorate.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸洛，召對，賜金紫。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited Luoyang, he was summoned to audience and granted gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Luoyang, Shi was called to audience and given gold-and-purple regalia.

sentences.zh: 史久在洛，因卜居，有亭榭竹樹之勝，優遊自得。

translations.literal: Shi had long been in Luoyang; he therefore chose a dwelling, with pavilions, terraces, bamboo, and trees of fine quality, and lived at leisure in contentment.
translations.idiomatic: Having settled in Luoyang for years, he chose a home graced with pavilions, bamboo, and trees, and lived there at ease.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: Before long he died, at the age of seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward, aged seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 所撰又有《太平寰宇記》二百卷，《總記傳》百三十卷，《坐知天下記》四十卷，《商顏雜錄》、《廣卓異記》各二十卷，《諸仙傳》二十五卷，《宋齊丘文傳》十三卷，《杏園集》、《李白別集》、《神仙宮殿窟宅記》各十卷，《掌上華夷圖》一卷。

translations.literal: His writings also included Comprehensive Geography in two hundred juan, General Record Biographies in one hundred thirty juan, Sit and Know the Empire in forty juan, Miscellaneous Records of Shangshan and Guang Records of Outstanding Worthies each in twenty juan, Biographies of Various Immortals in twenty-five juan, Collected Writings of Song Qiqiu in thirteen juan, Apricot Garden Collection, Separate Collection of Li Bai, and Record of Immortal Palaces, Caves, and Dwellings each in ten juan, and Pocket Map of China and the Barbarians in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: He also authored Comprehensive Geography (200 juan), General Record Biographies (130 juan), Sit and Know the Empire (40 juan), Miscellaneous Records of Shangshan and Guang Records of Outstanding Worthies (20 juan each), Biographies of Various Immortals (25 juan), Collected Writings of Song Qiqiu (13 juan), Apricot Garden Collection, Separate Collection of Li Bai, and Record of Immortal Palaces, Caves, and Dwellings (10 juan each), and Pocket Map of China and the Barbarians (1 juan).

sentences.zh: 又編己所著為《仙洞集》百卷。

translations.literal: He also compiled his own writings as Immortal Cave Collection in one hundred juan.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled his own works into Immortal Cave Collection (100 juan).

sentences.zh: 黃目淳化三年舉進士，補伊闕尉。

translations.literal: Huangmu passed the jinshi in the third year of Chunhua and was appointed district captain of Yique.
translations.idiomatic: Huangmu took the jinshi in Chunhua 3 and was made district captain of Yique.

sentences.zh: 遷大理寺丞、知壽安縣。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Shou'an County.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Shou'an County.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，徙知壁州，未行，上章言邊事，召對，拜殿中丞。

translations.literal: In the Xianping era, he was transferred to prefect of Bi Prefecture; before departing he memorialized on border affairs, was summoned to audience, and was appointed Palace Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianping era he was slated for Bizhou but, before leaving, memorialized on frontier affairs, was called to audience, and made palace vice director.

sentences.zh: 久之，直史館、知浚儀縣。

translations.literal: After some time, he served as straight officer of the Historiography Institute and magistrate of Junyi County.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was a straight officer of the historiography institute and magistrate of Junyi County.

sentences.zh: 俄上言曰：『伏以從政之原，州縣為急；

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized, saying: "I humbly consider that in the origin of governance, prefectures and counties are urgent;
translations.idiomatic: He soon memorialized: "I submit that the root of governance lies in the urgency of prefectures and counties;

sentences.zh: 親民之任，牧宰居先。

translations.literal: in duties that touch the people, prefects and magistrates should come first.
translations.idiomatic: and among duties that touch the people, prefects and magistrates must come first.

sentences.zh: 今朝官以數任除知州，簿尉以兩任入縣令，雖功過易見，而能否難明。

translations.literal: At present court officials are by several terms of service appointed prefects, and clerks and captains after two terms enter as county magistrates; though achievements and faults are easy to see, ability and incapacity are hard to make clear.
translations.idiomatic: Today court officials become prefects after a few terms and clerks and captains become county magistrates after two — merit and fault may be visible, but real capacity is hard to judge.

sentences.zh: 伏見唐開元二年選群官，有宏才通識、堪致理化者，授刺史、都督。

translations.literal: I humbly observe that in the second year of Kaiyuan under Tang, when selecting among the officials, those with broad talent, comprehensive knowledge, and capacity to bring about order and transformation were appointed prefects and regional commanders.
translations.idiomatic: I note that in Tang Kaiyuan 2 officials of broad talent and comprehensive insight fit to bring order and teach the people were made prefects and regional commanders.

sentences.zh: 又引新授縣令於宣政殿，試理人策一道，惟鄄城令袁濟及格，擢授醴泉令，餘二百人，且令赴任，十餘人並放令習學。

translations.literal: They also summoned newly appointed county magistrates to the Xuanzheng Hall and tested one policy essay on governing the people; only Yuan Ji, magistrate of Juancheng, passed, and was promoted and appointed magistrate of Liquan; of the remaining two hundred, some were ordered to take up their posts, and more than ten were all dismissed and ordered to study.
translations.idiomatic: Newly appointed county magistrates were also examined in the Xuanzheng Hall with one essay on governing the people; only Yuan Ji of Juancheng passed and was promoted to Liquan — of the other two hundred, some were sent to their posts, and more than ten were dismissed to continue their studies.

sentences.zh: 臣欲望自今審官院差知州，銓曹注縣令，候各及三二十人，一次引見於御前，試時務策一道。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes that from now on, when the Bureau of Review assigns prefects and the Bureau of Appointments registers county magistrates, once each group reaches twenty or thirty, they be once brought before the throne for audience and tested with one policy essay on current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that hereafter, whenever the bureau of review assigns prefects and the bureau of appointments registers magistrates, groups of twenty or thirty be brought before Your Majesty at once and tested with one essay on current affairs.

sentences.zh: 察言觀行，取其才識明於吏治、達於教化者充選；

translations.literal: Observe their words and watch their conduct, and select those whose talent and knowledge are clear in administration of affairs and reach to transformation and teaching to fill the appointments;
translations.idiomatic: Watch their words and conduct, and choose those clear in administration and adept at teaching and transforming the people;

sentences.zh: 其有不分曲直、罔辨是非者，或黜之厘務，或退守舊資。

translations.literal: those who cannot distinguish right from wrong and fail to discern what is and is not — either dismiss them to detailed duties or return them to their former rank.
translations.idiomatic: those who cannot tell right from wrong should be dismissed to routine duties or returned to their former rank.

sentences.zh: 如此，則官得其人，事無不治。』

translations.literal: If this is done, then offices will get the right men and no affair will go ungoverned."
translations.idiomatic: Then every post would have the right man and no affair would go untended."

sentences.zh: 上頗嘉其好古。

translations.literal: The emperor was quite pleased with his fondness for antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was rather pleased with his appeal to ancient precedent.

sentences.zh: 曆度支、鹽鐵判官，遷太常博士、京西轉運使。

translations.literal: He served as judge of the fiscal and salt-and-iron offices, was promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and transport commissioner for the Western Capital circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He served as judge of the fiscal and salt-and-iron offices, then became an erudite of the court of imperial sacrifices and transport commissioner for the western capital circuit.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，時真宗將幸洛，以供億務繁，起令蒞職。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother; at the time Zhenzong was about to visit Luoyang, and because supply duties were numerous and heavy, he was recalled from mourning and ordered to take up his post.
translations.idiomatic: When he went into mourning for his mother, Zhenzong was preparing to visit Luoyang; supply work was urgent and he was recalled to duty.

sentences.zh: 史尋卒，上復詔權奪。

translations.literal: Shi soon died; the emperor again ordered that mourning be suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Shi died soon after, and the emperor again authorized suspension of mourning.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符中，使契丹還，改工部員外郎、廣南西路轉運使。

translations.literal: In the Dazhong Xiangfu era, returning from an envoy mission to the Khitan, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and transport commissioner of the Guangnan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dazhong Xiangfu era, returning from a Khitan mission, he was made vice director of works and transport commissioner for the Guangnan West circuit.

sentences.zh: 就拜起居郎，改陝西轉運使，賜金紫。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed Court Secretary, transferred to transport commissioner of Shaanxi, and granted gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately made court secretary, then Shaanxi transport commissioner, and granted gold-and-purple regalia.

sentences.zh: 陳堯諮知永興，好以氣淩黃目，因表求解職，不許。

translations.literal: Chen Yaozi served as prefect of Yongxing and liked to overwhelm Huangmu with overbearing airs; Huangmu therefore memorialized requesting release from office, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yaozi, prefect of Yongxing, habitually browbeat Huangmu; Huangmu memorialized to be relieved, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 堯諮多縱恣不法，有密言其事者，詔黃目察之，得實以聞，堯諮坐罷龍圖閣職，徙知鄧州。

translations.literal: Yaozi was often reckless and lawless; someone secretly reported the matter, and an edict ordered Huangmu to investigate; finding the facts he reported them, and Yaozi was punished by removal from his Longtu Pavilion post and transfer to prefect of Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yaozi was widely lawless and overbearing; after a secret report the court ordered Huangmu to investigate. He confirmed the charges and Yaozi was stripped of his Longtu Pavilion post and sent to Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 八年，黃目入判三司三勾院。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Huangmu entered to judge the Three Check Office of the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Huangmu was made judge of the Three Offices Three Check Office.

sentences.zh: 天禧初，馬元方奏黃目職事不舉，遂分三勾院，以三人掌之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxi, Ma Yuanfang memorialized that Huangmu was not performing his duties, and the Three Check Office was then divided, with three men put in charge.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianxi, Ma Yuanfang charged that Huangmu was neglecting his duties; the Three Check Office was split and placed under three officials.

sentences.zh: 黃目罷任，奉朝請。

translations.literal: Huangmu was removed from his post and attended court as gentleman-at-attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Huangmu was relieved and kept on as a court gentleman.

sentences.zh: 逾月，拜兵部員外郎、知制誥，充會靈觀判官。

translations.literal: After more than a month, he was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of War and Drafting Edict, and served as judge of the Huiling Temple.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he was made vice director of war and drafter of edicts, with concurrent duty as judge of the Huiling Temple.

sentences.zh: 黃目屬辭淹緩，朝議以為不稱職。

translations.literal: Huangmu's drafting was slow and prolix, and court opinion held that he was unfit for the post.
translations.idiomatic: Huangmu's prose was slow and overblown, and the court judged him unfit for the post.

sentences.zh: 時以盛度知京府，辭不拜，即遷黃目右諫議大夫、權知開封府，度為會靈觀判官，兩換其任。

translations.literal: At the time Sheng Du was appointed to govern the capital prefecture but declined to accept; Huangmu was immediately transferred to Right Remonstrance Censor and acting prefect of Kaifeng, and Du was made judge of the Huiling Temple — the two exchanged their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Du had been slated for the capital prefecture but declined; Huangmu was made right remonstrance censor and acting prefect of Kaifeng while Du took the Huiling Temple judgeship — the two men traded places.

sentences.zh: 仁宗升儲，拜給事中兼左庶子。

translations.literal: When Renzong was established as heir apparent, Huangmu was appointed Attendant Censor and concurrently Left Sub-mentor.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong was named heir apparent, Huangmu was made attendant censor and left sub-mentor.

sentences.zh: 入內副都知張繼能，嘗以公事請托黃目，至是未申謝，事敗，降左諫議大夫、知荊南府。

translations.literal: Inner Deputy Director Zhang Jineng had once solicited Huangmu on official business; at this time he had not yet presented thanks, the affair was exposed, and Huangmu was demoted to Left Remonstrance Censor and prefect of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jineng, inner deputy director, had once asked Huangmu for an official favor; when the matter collapsed before Jineng could even thank him, Huangmu was demoted to left remonstrance censor and prefect of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 明年，復為給事中，徙潭州。

translations.literal: The next year he was again made Attendant Censor and transferred to Tan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was restored as attendant censor and transferred to Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 長沙月給，減於荊渚，特詔增之，又諭以兵賦繁綜寄任之意。

translations.literal: The monthly stipend at Changsha was less than at Jingzhou; a special edict increased it, and he was also instructed on the meaning of the heavy trust placed in him for military and tax affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Changsha's monthly allowance was lower than Jingnan's; an edict specially raised it and explained the weight of military and fiscal responsibility entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 五年，代還，知審官院。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, returning at the end of his term, he was made director of the Bureau of Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he completed his tour and was put in charge of the bureau of review.

sentences.zh: 黃目以風疾題品乖當，改知通進、銀臺司兼門下封駁事。

translations.literal: Because of illness Huangmu's evaluations of candidates were improper; he was transferred to director of the Memorials Gateway and Silver Terrace Office with concurrent duty over gate seals and review.
translations.idiomatic: Illness led his candidate evaluations astray; he was reassigned to the Memorials Gateway and Silver Terrace Office with concurrent gate seal and review duties.

sentences.zh: 數月，求外任，得知亳州。

translations.literal: After several months he sought an outside appointment and was made prefect of Bo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Within months he sought a provincial post and was made prefect of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 俄而幼子死，聞訃慟絕，所疾加甚，卒，年五十六。

translations.literal: Soon his youngest son died; on hearing the news he was so stricken with grief that he collapsed, his illness worsened, and he died at the age of fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: When his youngest son died, the news broke him with grief, his illness worsened, and he died at fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 錄其子理國為衛尉寺丞，定國為大理評事。

translations.literal: His sons Liguo and Dingguo were recorded for appointment as Vice Director of the Guard Command and Reviewing Officer of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Liguo and Dingguo were granted posts as vice director in the guard command and reviewing officer in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 黃目面柔簡默，為吏處劇，亦無敗事。

translations.literal: Huangmu had a gentle face and was brief and quiet in speech; as an official he handled difficult matters and also had no failures.
translations.idiomatic: Huangmu was mild-faced and sparing of words; even in heavy posts he never failed.

sentences.zh: 有集五十卷，又撰《學海搜奇錄》四十卷，《聖朝郡國志》二十卷。

translations.literal: He had collected writings in fifty juan, and also authored Sea of Learning: Search for Wonders in forty juan and Gazetteer of Commanderies of the Holy Dynasty in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings ran to fifty juan; he also wrote Sea of Learning: Search for Wonders (40 juan) and Gazetteer of Commanderies of the Holy Dynasty (20 juan).

sentences.zh: 黃目兄黃裳，弟黃庭，黃裳孫滋，並進士及第。

translations.literal: Huangmu's elder brother Huang Shang, younger brother Huang Ting, and Huang Shang's grandson Zi all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Huang Shang, younger brother Huang Ting, and Huang Shang's grandson Zi all took the jinshi.

sentences.zh: 黃裳、黃庭皆至太常博士。

translations.literal: Huang Shang and Huang Ting both reached Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Shang and Huang Ting both rose to erudite of the court of imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 柴成務

translations.literal: Chai Chengwu
translations.idiomatic: Chai Chengwu

sentences.zh: 柴成務，字寶臣，曹州濟陰人也。

translations.literal: Chai Chengwu, courtesy name Baochen, was a native of Jiyin in Cao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Chengwu, styled Baochen, came from Jiyin in Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 父自牧，舉進士，能詩，至兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: His father Zimu passed the jinshi examination, could compose poetry, and reached Vice Director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zimu was a jinshi and a poet who rose to vice director of war.

sentences.zh: 成務，乾德中京府拔解，太宗素知其名，首薦之，遂中進士甲科，解褐陝州軍事推官。

translations.literal: Chengwu, in the Qiande era passing the capital prefecture preliminary examination, Taizong had long known his name and first recommended him; he then passed the jinshi in the top tier and took his first post as military aide of Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiande, Chengwu passed the capital preliminary; Taizong, who had long known his name, recommended him first on the list, and he took top honors on the jinshi, entering service as military aide of Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 改曹、單觀察推官，遷大理寺丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to investigative aide of Cao and Shan and promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He became investigative aide for Cao and Shan prefectures, then vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 太平興國五年，轉太常丞，充陝西轉運副使，賜緋，再遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, served as deputy transport commissioner of Shaanxi, was granted crimson robes, and was promoted again to Attending Censor of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 5 he became vice director of the court of imperial sacrifices and deputy transport commissioner for Shaanxi, received crimson robes, and was raised to palace attending censor.

sentences.zh: 八年，與供奉官葛彥恭使河南，案行遙堤。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, together with Palatial Attendant Ge Yanchong he was dispatched to Henan to inspect and traverse the remote dikes.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he and palatial attendant Ge Yanchong toured Henan to inspect the remote dikes.

sentences.zh: 曆知果、蘇二州，就為兩浙轉運使，改戶部員外郎、直史館，賜金紫。

translations.literal: He served in succession as prefect of Guo and Su Prefectures, was then made transport commissioner of Liangzhe, was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and straight officer of the Historiography Institute, and was granted gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Guo and Suzhou in turn, became Liangzhe transport commissioner, then vice director of revenue and straight officer of the historiography institute, with gold-and-purple regalia.

sentences.zh: 入為戶部判官、遷本曹郎中。

translations.literal: He entered court as judge of the Ministry of Revenue and was promoted to Director of that bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as revenue judge and rose to director of that bureau.

sentences.zh: 太宗選郎官為少卿監，以成務為光祿少卿。

translations.literal: Taizong selected bureau directors to serve as vice ministers of directorates and appointed Chengwu Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong tapped bureau directors for vice-minister posts in the directorates, Chengwu was made vice minister of the court of imperial entertainments.

sentences.zh: 俄奉使高麗，遠俗尚拘忌，以月日未利拜恩，稽留朝使，成務貽書，往反開諭大體，國人信服，事具《高麗傳》。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent on mission to Goryeo; the distant customs still observed taboos, and because the day and month were not auspicious for receiving thanks, they detained the court envoys; Chengwu sent letters back and forth explaining the larger principle, and the people of the country came to trust and accept — the affair is fully recorded in the Goryeo Annals.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went as envoy to Goryeo. Local custom was bound by taboos, and because the day was inauspicious for accepting imperial favor they detained the mission; Chengwu exchanged letters until both sides grasped the larger courtesy, and the Koreans were won over — the full account is in the Goryeo Annals.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，為京東轉運使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua he was made transport commissioner of Jingdong.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua 2 he became Jingdong transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 會宋州河決，成務上言：『河水所經地肥澱，願免其租稅，勸民種藝。』

translations.literal: When the Yellow River broke its banks at Song Prefecture, Chengwu memorialized: "The land through which the river waters pass is enriched by sediment; I wish its rent and tax may be remitted and the people encouraged to plant crops."
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River broke through at Songzhou, Chengwu memorialized: "The flooded land is rich with silt; I ask that rent and tax be remitted and the people urged to farm."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 召拜司封郎中、知制誥，賜錢三十萬。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Director of the Bureau of Awards and Drafting Edict, and was granted three hundred thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as director of the bureau of awards and drafter of edicts, with a grant of three hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 時呂蒙正為宰相，嘗與之聯外姻，避嫌辭職，不許。

translations.literal: At the time Lü Mengzheng was chief minister; he had once been related by marriage to Chengwu, and Chengwu avoided conflict by requesting resignation, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Lü Mengzheng was a former in-law; Chengwu tried to resign to avoid suspicion, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 俄與魏庠同知京朝官考課。

translations.literal: Soon he and Wei Ku jointly directed the performance review of capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined Wei Ku in directing the performance review of capital officials.

sentences.zh: 四年，又與庠同知給事中事，凡制敕有所不便者，許封駁以聞。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he again joined Ku in jointly administering the affairs of supervising censor, and whenever an edict or order was inconvenient, they were permitted to seal and return it with a report.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he again joined Wei Ku in jointly administering the affairs of supervising censor; whenever an edict or order was unsuitable, they were permitted to seal and return it with a report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 蜀寇平，使峽路安撫，改左諫議大夫、知河中府。

translations.literal: When the Shu rebels were pacified, he was sent as pacification commissioner of the Gorges route, then changed to Left Remonstrance Censor and prefect of Hezhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After the Shu rebels were pacified, he was sent as pacification commissioner of the Gorges route, then appointed Left Remonstrance Censor and prefect of Hezhong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時銀、夏未寧，蒲津當饋免之衝，事皆辦集，得脫戶八百家以附籍。

translations.literal: At the time Yin and Xia were not yet settled; Pujin lay on the route of grain transport and exemption, and he handled all affairs so that they were gathered—obtaining eight hundred households who had escaped registration to be entered on the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and Xia were not yet settled; Pujin lay on the critical route for grain transport and tax exemptions. He handled every matter efficiently and brought eight hundred unregistered households back onto the tax rolls.

sentences.zh: 府城街陌頗隘狹，成務曰：『國家承平已久，如車駕臨幸，何以駐千乘萬騎邪？』

translations.literal: The streets and lanes of the prefectural city were rather narrow and cramped. Chengwu said: 'The state has enjoyed peace for a long time—if the imperial carriage should visit, how could a thousand chariots and ten thousand horsemen be stationed?'
translations.idiomatic: The streets of the prefectural city were narrow and cramped. Chengwu said: "The realm has been at peace for a long time. If the imperial carriage should visit, how could a thousand chariots and ten thousand horsemen be quartered here?"

sentences.zh: 乃奏撤民廬以廣之。

translations.literal: He thereupon memorialized to remove commoners' houses to widen them.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to remove private dwellings and widen the streets.

sentences.zh: 其後祀汾陰，果留蹕河中，衢路顯敞，咸以為便。

translations.literal: Afterward, when sacrifices were performed at Fenyin, the emperor indeed halted at Hezhong; the thoroughfares were open and broad, and all considered it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the emperor performed sacrifices at Fenyin, he indeed halted at Hezhong. The thoroughfares were open and broad, and everyone found the change convenient.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，遷給事中、知梓州。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong succeeded to the throne, Chengwu was transferred to Supervising Censor and made prefect of Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong succeeded to the throne, Chengwu was promoted to Supervising Censor and appointed prefect of Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾代還，又遣知青州，表求俟永熙陵復土畢之任。

translations.literal: Before long his replacement arrived and he returned; he was again sent to administer Qingzhou, and submitted a memorial asking to wait until the restoration of Yongxi Mausoleum was complete before taking up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his replacement arrived and he returned to court. He was again dispatched to administer Qingzhou and asked in a memorial to delay taking up the post until restoration work at Yongxi Mausoleum was complete.

sentences.zh: 旋受詔與錢若水等同修《太宗實錄》，書成，知揚州。

translations.literal: Shortly he received an edict to compile the Veritable Records of Taizong together with Qian Ruoshui and others; when the work was finished, he was made prefect of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he received an edict to compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Taizong together with Qian Ruoshui and others. When the work was finished, he was appointed prefect of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 入判尚書刑部，本司小吏倨慢，成務怒而笞之，吏擊登聞鼓訴冤，有詔問狀。

translations.literal: He entered to judge the Ministry of Punishments of the Imperial Secretariat; a petty clerk of the office was arrogant and disrespectful, and Chengwu in anger had him beaten with the rod. The clerk struck the Court of Imperial Complaints drum to plead injustice, and an edict ordered an inquiry into the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed to judge the Ministry of Punishments. A petty clerk of the office was arrogant and disrespectful; Chengwu in anger had him beaten with the rod. The clerk struck the Court of Imperial Complaints drum to plead injustice, and the emperor ordered an inquiry.

sentences.zh: 成務歎曰：『忝為長官，杖一胥而被劾，何面目據堂決事邪！』

translations.literal: Chengwu sighed and said: 'I am disgraced to hold the post of chief—beaten one clerk and am impeached; with what face can I sit in court and decide affairs!'
translations.idiomatic: Chengwu sighed and said: "I hold the post of chief official, yet I beat one clerk and am impeached. With what face can I sit in court and decide affairs?"

sentences.zh: 乃求解職。

translations.literal: He thereupon requested to be relieved of his post.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon asked to resign his post.

sentences.zh: 景德初，卒，年七十一。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde he died, age seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jingde (1004) he died, at the age of seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 成務有詞學，博聞稽古，善談論，好諧笑，士人重其文雅。

translations.literal: Chengwu had literary learning, broad knowledge and investigation of antiquity, was skilled in discourse, loved witty banter, and scholar-officials valued his refined culture.
translations.idiomatic: Chengwu was learned in letters, widely read in antiquity, skilled in conversation, and fond of witty banter. Scholar-officials esteemed his refined culture.

sentences.zh: 然為郡乏廉稱，時論惜之。

translations.literal: Yet in governing prefectures he lacked a reputation for integrity, and opinion of the time regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as a prefect he lacked a reputation for integrity, and contemporaries regretted it.

sentences.zh: 文集二十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works of twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works of twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 成務年六十六始有子，比卒，才六歲，授奉禮郎，名貽範，後為國子博士。

translations.literal: Chengwu was sixty-six before he had a son; when he died the boy was only six. He was granted Ceremonial Officer, named Yifan, and later became Erudite of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Chengwu was sixty-six before he had a son; when he died the boy was only six. The boy was granted Ceremonial Officer, named Yifan, and later became Erudite of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 論曰：泌述唐、漢之治，台符陳商、周之鑒，曆布腹心，奏議反覆論當世事，盡言無隱。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Bi set forth the governance of Tang and Han; Taifu cited the lessons of Shang and Zhou. They repeatedly laid bare their innermost thoughts, and in memorials debated current affairs back and forth, speaking fully without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: Xie Bi expounded the governance of Tang and Han; Zhu Taifu cited the lessons of Shang and Zhou. They repeatedly spoke from the heart, and in memorials debated current affairs without reserve.

sentences.zh: 何建五議，綸摭十事，皆切於輔治。

translations.literal: He proposed five measures; Lun gathered ten matters—all pressing on assisting governance.
translations.idiomatic: Sun He proposed five measures; Qi Lun gathered ten matters—all aimed squarely at assisting good government.

sentences.zh: 何勤接士類，綸樂於薦士，皆足以儀表當世者也。

translations.literal: He diligently received men of the scholar class; Lun delighted in recommending scholars—both were sufficient to serve as models for their age.
translations.idiomatic: Sun He diligently received men of the scholar class; Qi Lun delighted in recommending talent—both were fit to serve as models for their age.

sentences.zh: 去華頗尚氣節，而能作成後進；

translations.literal: Quhua rather valued integrity and could nurture those who came after;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Quhua valued integrity and nurtured those who came after him;

sentences.zh: 黃目屬辭淹緩，而著述浩瀚；

translations.literal: Huangmu's composition was slow and dilatory, yet his writings were vast;
translations.idiomatic: Le Huangmu composed slowly, yet his writings were vast;

sentences.zh: 成務寡清白之操，而專對不辱，俱有足稱者焉。

translations.literal: Chengwu lacked a reputation for pure conduct, yet in special audiences he was not disgraced—all had qualities worth praising.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Chengwu lacked a reputation for pure conduct, yet in diplomatic audiences he did not disgrace his office. Each had qualities worth praising.
